item.title: Explicit Error Term in the Chebotarev Density Theorem for Function Fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.28155v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an explicit error term in the Chebotarev Density Theorem for finite generically Galois \'etale morphisms of affine varieties over finite fields, under a mild condition on their size. The error term generalises the known results for curves, and depends only on invariants of the varieties. We present several applications to the explicit error term. We apply it to existence problems, and to the Bateman-Horn conjecture over finite fields.
item.dc:creator: Ido Benbenishty Shpilka

item.title: The Tate Conjecture in Positive Characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2611.28178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{Z}(n)$ be Bloch's cycle complex and $\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ be the complex that compute continuous \'etale cohomology. Kahn observed that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to the map $\mathcal{Z}(n)\otimes\mathbb{Z}(0)^c\to\mathbb{Z}(n)^c$ being isomorphism. Later, Kahn found that the Tate conjecture for a finite field is equivalent to $\Omega_\ell(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\in DM^{\text{eff}}_{\text{\'et}}(k)$, where $\Omega_\ell$ is the right adjoint of the $\ell$-adic realisation functor. In this note, using the Dwyer-Greenlees equivalence between $\ell$-completed objects and $\ell$-torsion objects, we prove that $\Omega_\ell(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\in DM^{\text{eff}}_{\text{\'et}}(k)$, and consequently, based on Kahn's early work, the Tate conjecture at positive characteristics.
item.dc:creator: Yunhao Sun

item.title: Reduction types of curves in tame extensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.28255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $C/K$ be a curve of genus $g\geq 1$ over a discretely valued field $K$ with algebraically closed residue field. In this paper, we study the behaviour of the reduction type of $C$ under finite tame extensions. If $L/K$ is a tame extension of degree $n$, we give sufficient conditions on the reduction type $R$ of $C$ so that the reduction type of the base change $C_L$ is uniquely determined by $R$ and $n$. In particular, if $C$ has abelian and toric ranks zero, then $R$ satisfies these conditions. We also give an algorithm to compute the possibilities for the reduction type of $C_L$ given only $R$ and $n$. The main method involves studying harmonic covers of graphs with a cyclic action. As a result, we obtain a characterisation of tame curves with potentially good reduction in terms of their reduction type, and a new proof of a result by Liu-Lorenzini-Raynaud regarding the non-realisability of certain reduction types.
item.dc:creator: J\'ulia Mart\'inez-Mar\'in

item.title: Recurrence formulas for Taylor expansions at CM points on genus-one and genus-two Shimura curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.28257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a general differential equation relating the expansion of a weight-two eigenform $f$ on a Shimura curve to the Schwarzian derivative $\mathcal{R}$ associated with $f$. When the quotient $X/W$ has genus zero, we introduce a Hauptmodul $u$ and obtain a coupled system of differential equations involving $f$, $\mathcal{R}$, and $u$. Geometric information, including local constraints on the poles of $\mathcal{R}$, together with the initial coefficients of the expansion of $f$, determine all the parameters in the system. We apply this method to all twelve weight-two eigenforms on Shimura curves $X_0^N(1)$ of genus one or two, obtaining explicit recurrence formulas for their Taylor expansions at selected CM points, conditional on the numerically recognized initial coefficients. As an application, we use the coefficients obtained from the recurrence to compute the Shimura uniformization $\Phi: \operatorname{Jac}(X)\to E$ to high precision and identify a large family of CM points on the associated elliptic curves $E$.
item.dc:creator: Jingxuan Geng

item.title: Improved bounds for the binary Chowla conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.28392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the M\"obius function $\mu$ and every fixed $0 < \epsilon < 1$, we prove \[ \sum_{n \le x} \mu(n) \mu(n + 1) \ll_{\epsilon} \frac{x}{(\log x)^{1 - \epsilon}}. \] This improves on OpenAI's recent bound of $x/(\log x)^c$, where $c > 0$ is a tiny absolute constant. The proof echoes the graph expansion framework of Helfgott, Radziwill, and Pilatte on the logarithmic Chowla conjecture, earlier Fourier analytic methods of Matom\"aki, Radziwill, and Tao on the Chowla conjecture on average, as well as work of Ter\"av\"ainen and the author for M\"obius on shifted primes. This also yields an improved result, \[ \sum_{p \le x} \mu(p + 2) \ll_{\epsilon} \frac{\pi(x)}{(\log x)^{1/2 - \epsilon}}. \] Specifically, we refine the determinant approach from the Poisson-Dirichlet law for prime predecessors. We replace the averaged prime weights of L\"u-Wang-Wu with an exact partition of prime intervals. Once sieving out exceptional integers, this enables uniform cancellation with arbitrary log power savings.
item.dc:creator: Jared Duker Lichtman

item.title: Uniform counting of quadratic fields with local conditions
item.description: arXiv:2611.28448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We sharpen the uniform counting estimates of Bhargava, Thorne, and the author for quadratic fields with prescribed local conditions. Combining the Burgess and P\'olya--Vinogradov bounds, we improve the dependence of the error term on the primes supporting the local conditions and make explicit the factors previously absorbed into an arbitrary $\epsilon$-power of their product. The resulting estimate has an absolute implied constant.
item.dc:creator: Takashi Taniguchi

item.title: Stepanov's method and uniform sumset estimates in arbitrary finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.28533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $A<\mathbb F_q^\times$ be a proper multiplicative subgroup that generates $\mathbb F_q$ over its prime field. We prove that \[ |A+A|\ge \tfrac18|A|^{3/2} \] whenever $|A|<q^{2/3}$, uniformly in the characteristic and extension degree, without quantitative restrictions on intersections with proper subfields. Moreover, in contrast with what is expected in prime fields, we show that no uniform bound with exponent larger than $5/3$ holds in $\mathbb F_q$ even for $|A| \approx q^{1/2}$. The proof's key idea is to run the prime-field Stepanov method in reverse, constructing an auxiliary polynomial whose specialization vanishes identically instead of requiring it to be nonzero.
item.dc:creator: Albert Cochrane, Todd Cochrane, Craig Spencer

item.title: A two-sided continued-fraction criterion for the Erd\H{o}s-Moser equation and Erd\H{o}s's 1949 problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.28637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a two-sided continued-fraction criterion for the Erd\H{o}s--Moser equation $1^k+2^k+\dots+(m-1)^k=m^k$. Writing $m=k/\log 2+3/2+\gamma_m/m$, Gallot, Moree and Zudilin showed that a solution yields a convergent of $\log 2/(2N)$, for a known divisor $N$ of $k$, followed by a large partial quotient. We show that an explicit two-sided estimate for $\gamma_m$, from our earlier centre-of-mass work, restricts this partial quotient, for each value of $\gcd(k/N,2m-3)$, to two consecutive values, or to three in the exceptional case that an integer lies in an explicit interval of relative length $O(1/m)$. This excludes the first index left open by their computation and, without extending their continued-fraction computation, raises the lower bound for a nontrivial solution from $m>2.71\cdot 10^{1667658416}$ to $m>6.26\cdot 10^{1667658425}$. The same criterion gives an effective form of the asymptotic results of Best and te Riele on Erd\H{o}s's 1949 problem on the largest term of $1^n+\dots+(m-1)^n$. We determine all 50 pairs $(m,n)$ with $m<10^{399}$ for which $(m-2)^n<(m-1)^n/2$ and $1^n+\dots+(m-1)^n>m^n$; in particular, the smallest example found by Best and te Riele in 1976 is the smallest such pair, a question they had left open. For $n<0.69\cdot 10^{399}$ we also determine the 51 elements of O'Bryant's exceptional set $A_2$ and all 101 terms of OEIS A129935 below this bound, one of them not previously listed, and settle several conjectures recorded in the OEIS. Finally, using only the upper bound in our estimate for $\gamma_m$ and its positivity, we show that the second part of Erd\H{o}s's problem, the existence of infinitely many such pairs, is equivalent to the infinitude of $A_2$ and to the existence of infinitely many even-index convergents $p_j/q_j$ of $\log 2$ with $p_j$ even, $q_j$ odd and $q_j(q_j\log 2-p_j)<\Theta(q_j)$, where $\Theta(q)=(\log 2)/3+O(q^{-2})$ is explicit.
item.dc:creator: Elham Mehdi-Nezhad, Amir M. Rahimi

item.title: Exact-Order Mellin Transfer and Prime-Support Filtrations
item.description: arXiv:2611.28769v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a unified exact-order Mellin transfer principle that converts the multiplicity of a critical Mellin pole into arithmetic prime-support depth. For an exact-order M\"obius transform in lattice dimension $\ell$, a base pole of order $r$ at $s=\ell/2$ satisfies \[ \ord_{s=\ell/2}\widehat{\mathscr P_{N,\ell}H}=\omega(N)-r. \] The complete Jordan--Mellin jet is explicit, and its first surviving coefficient selects the canonical weight $W(N)=\prod_{p\mid N}\log p$. After the corresponding jet normalization, this weight governs a kernel-independent moving-support law and a mod-Poisson regime. With simultaneous splitting marks in finite Galois extensions, the same weight yields a multivariate polynomial whose mixed coefficients are reciprocal compositum degrees; it recovers pairwise intersection degrees and, under a full-rank hypothesis, also governs the coupled saddle and large-deviation geometry. In spectral geometry, a two-variable family attached to any positive self-adjoint elliptic operator has a transverse normal crossing whose parameter jets generate every higher critical pole order; exact-order dilation therefore realizes every positive prime-support depth. An explicit Bernoulli--Barnes/Barnes--Epstein model shows how a pole collision shifts the finite critical layer from one-prime to two-prime support. Thus arithmetic support, Galois compositum data, and spectral pole geometry arise from one exact-order Mellin mechanism.
item.dc:creator: Dongkyu Lim, Abdelmejid Bayad

item.title: Congruences modulo powers of $2$ and $3$ for Lin's function $\text{PDO}_t(n)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.28840v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\text{PDO}_t(n)$ denote the total number of tagged parts over all partitions of $n$ into odd parts with designated summands. Confirming a conjecture of Singh and Barman (2025), Tang (2026) recently proved that $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{2m-1}n)\equiv0\pmod{2^{3m+1}}$ for all $m\geq1$ and $n\geq0$. Using elementary techniques, we obtain explicit polynomial expansions for the generating functions of $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{m+2}n)$, and we use them to determine $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{k}n)$ modulo one further power of $2$. More precisely, we show that the quotient of $\text{PDO}_t(3\times2^{k}n)$ by the relevant power of $2$ is odd exactly when $n$ is an odd square, or $2$, $3$ or $6$ times an odd square, depending on $k$. As a consequence, we obtain several new infinite families of congruences modulo arbitrary powers of $2$, such as \[ \text{PDO}_t\bigl(3\times4^{m}(3n+2)\bigr)\equiv0\pmod{2^{3m+4}}, \] and \[\text{PDO}_t\bigl(3\times4^{m}(6n+5)\bigr)\equiv0\pmod{2^{3m+5}}. \] We also obtain an analogous improvement of a result of Li and Tang (2026) modulo powers of $3$, and an infinite family of internal congruences modulo powers of $2$.
item.dc:creator: Manjil P. Saikia

item.title: Elliptic curves with torsion Z/5: exact rank four over Q(k) and rank at least five infinitely often
item.description: arXiv:2611.28977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give two elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}(k)$ with torsion group $\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}$ and rank exactly $4$, with four explicit independent points. The upper bounds come from reducing the relevant elliptic surfaces modulo suitable primes and are unconditional. They match the known lower bound for the generic rank with this torsion, due to Eroshkin, and are not isomorphic to Eroshkin's curve or to each other: their parametrising maps to $X_1(5)$ have degree $8$ instead of $12$, the constructions are dihedral rather than biquadratic, and their branch loci differ. In each case, two of the points come from a ``doubling'' step in the spirit of Jaswal. Adding one further condition to the second curve, coming from a quadratic twist over an intermediate conic, gives a fifth independent point over a genus-one curve of rank two. Hence there are infinitely many elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with torsion $\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z}$ and rank at least $5$, improving the known bound $C(\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z})\ge 4$ to $C(\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z})\ge 5$.
item.dc:creator: Andrej Dujella, Juan Carlos Peral

item.title: Improved Omega results for Riesz sums of a class of $L$-functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.28981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a general class of $L$-functions satisfying functional equations with multiple gamma factors, and establish sharper lower bounds for the error terms associated with the Riesz sums of their coefficients. By integrating the resonance method with Riesz smoothing, we improve upon previously known omega results for the corresponding Riesz sums. We prove these estimates within a unified axiomatic framework under a precise set of hypotheses. Our general theorem can be applied to several classical arithmetic problems, including the $k$-fold Piltz divisor function $d_{\mathbb{K},k}(n)$ over a number field $\mathbb{K}$, as well as the lattice point counting functions for the circle, ellipse, and sphere problems. In particular, we sharpen the classical $\Omega$-bound for the error in counting lattice points in the ellipse $u^2+5v^2\le x$, strengthening a result of Nowak. Moreover, for the smoothed error terms corresponding to the divisor and circle problems, we improve upon previously known $\Omega$-bounds by increasing the exponent of the $\log\log x$ factor and sharpening the $\log\log\log x$ dependence by replacing exponential decay factors of the form $\exp(-c\sqrt{\log\log\log x})$ in previous results with an explicit polynomial power of $\log\log\log x$.
item.dc:creator: Arindam Roy, Jagannath Sahoo, Akshaa Vatwani

item.title: On derived Galois deformation rings in characteristic 0 and a conjecture of Venkatesh
item.description: arXiv:2611.28988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Pi$ be a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of $\operatorname{GL}_n$ over a CM field $F$, and $\rho$ its associated Galois representation in characteristic 0. With mild assumptions, we use the Taylor--Wiles method to define a free action of the potentially semistable derived deformation ring of $\rho$ on the $\Pi$-part of the $p$-adic cohomology of $\operatorname{GL}_n/F$, confirming a prediction of Venkatesh. As a key step, we establish an equivalence between the derived deformation ring of $\rho$ with the completion at the point corresponding to $\rho$ of the derived deformation ring of the mod $p$ reduction $\bar{\rho}$, generalising well-known results by Kisin.
item.dc:creator: Douglas Molin

item.title: A bound for Stieltjes constants of the Riemann zeta function
item.description: arXiv:2611.29049v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The coefficients appearing in the Laurent expansion of the Riemann zeta function are known as the Stieltjes constants and are denoted by $\gamma_n$. Several authors, including Berndt, Matsuoka, Williams and Zhang, and Saad Eddin, have investigated upper bounds for $|\gamma_n|$, with the best known result due to Pauli and Saidak \cite{MR4671618}. In 2003, based on numerical evidence, Kreminski \cite{MR1972742} conjectured that Matsuoka's bound \cite{MR827790} could be considerably improved. Motivated by this conjecture, we employ the saddle-point method to derive an asymptotic formula for the Stieltjes constants, with the saddle point expressed explicitly in terms of the Lambert $W$-function. The resulting formula yields an asymptotic upper bound of the correct order of magnitude. Moreover, the resulting bound is consistent with the conjecture of Farr, Pauli, and Saidak \cite{MR4280128}.
item.dc:creator: Omprakash Atale, Suraj Singh Khurana

item.title: A ring of symmetric Hermitian modular forms of degree $2$ with integral Fourier coefficients II
item.description: arXiv:2611.29098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We exhibit 24 homogeneous generators for the graded \(\Z\)-algebra of symmetric Hermitian modular forms of degree 2 over \(\Q(i)\) with integral Fourier coefficients, where the weight \(k\) is even and the character is \(\det^{k/2}\). We prove that 24 is the minimum number of algebra generators. For the subalgebra in weights divisible by 4, Kurihara reduced the generating set given in our earlier work to 11 forms. We show that 13 further forms generate the direct sum of the components in weights congruent to 2 modulo 4 as a module over this subalgebra. For \(p=2\) and \(p=3\), we show that the ring of Fourier expansions modulo \(p\) is a polynomial ring over \(\F_p\) generated by the reductions of 4 forms of weights \(8,12,12,16\). We also record the diagonal Sturm bound \(\lfloor k/8\rfloor\) modulo every prime \(p\) and verify its sharpness in every even weight \(k\ne2\).
item.dc:creator: Toshiyuki Kikuta

item.title: On the number theory of the Greeks. I. The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
item.description: arXiv:2611.29380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article we present Euclid's fundamental theorem of number theory and give evidence for the claim that this theorem, which is largely unknown today, was as familiar to number theorists before Gauss as the Gaussian version of the fundamental theorem is to us.
item.dc:creator: Franz Lemmermeyer

item.title: On the Number Theory of the Greeks. II. Gauss's Lemmas and Riesz Domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.29386v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the second part of our article on Euclid's four number theorem we start from the notion of incommensurability and take a closer look at irrationality proofs for algebraic numbers. Along the way we encounter Gauss's Lemma, integral closure and Dedekind's Prague theorem, and finally we arrive back at the four number theorem.
item.dc:creator: Franz Lemmermeyer

item.title: Explicit exponent bounds for sums of consecutive powers
item.description: arXiv:2611.29398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $x^k+(x+1)^k=y^n$, where $x,y,k,n$ are positive integers with $k\ge2$ and $n\ge3$. We prove that $n<52k^2\log(2k)\log^2(50k)$ for odd $k$ and $n<216k\log^2(2500k)$ for even $k$. For odd $k$, an exact valuation formula reduces the problem to a linear form in two real logarithms. For even $k$, we use factorization in $\mathbb Z[i]$ and a bound of Yamada. When $k=5$, we prove that the original exponent $n$ is one of the 34 primes between $23$ and $181$, inclusive. Every solution satisfies $2x+1=u^n$ with $u>10^{1000}$. A gap between successive rational approximations to $2^{-4/n}$, together with the Thue--Siegel principle, gives at most four solutions for each of $n=23,29$ and at most three for each larger prime in this range. Thus there are at most 104 positive integer triples $(x,y,n)$ in the quintic case. All bounds are unconditional.
item.dc:creator: \'Akos Pint\'er

item.title: Shifted moments of angular Hecke $L$-functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.29401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish upper bounds for shifted moments of angular Hecke $L$-function over imaginary quadratic number fields of class number one under the generalized Riemann hypothesis. The result is used to derive bounds for moments of angular Hecke character sums.
item.dc:creator: Peng Gao

item.title: Sharp tails for arguments of Dirichlet $L$-functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.29424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $t$ be uniform on $[T,2T]$, let $\chi$ be a Dirichlet character modulo $q$, and set $X=\Im\log L(1/2+it,\chi)$ and $Q=\sum_{p\le T,\,p\nmid q}1/p$. For fixed $K,\theta_0>0$, uniformly in $q\le T^{\theta_0}$, $\chi$, and $0\le V\le KQ$, each signed tail $\Pr\{\pm X>V\}$ has order $\sqrt Q\,(V+\sqrt Q)^{-1}\exp(-V^2/Q)$. In particular, for $S(t)=\pi^{-1}\arg\zeta(1/2+it)$ and $0\le V\le K\log\log T$, each tail $\Pr\{\pm S(t)>V\}$ has order $\sqrt{\log\log T}\,(V+\sqrt{\log\log T})^{-1}\exp(-\pi^2V^2/\log\log T)$. For $|v|\le KQ$, the probability that $X$ lies in a fixed-width interval centered at $v$ has order $Q^{-1/2}\exp(-v^2/Q)$ whenever the width is sufficiently large. The upper bound holds for every fixed positive width. We also obtain matching bounds of order $\exp(k^2Q)$ for the means of $\exp(\pm2kX)$ for fixed $k>0$. The proof begins with a one-sided polynomial bound for each sign, using Alp\"oge's zero-location theorem at the primitive inducing conductor. A weighted comparison with a sum over primes controls departures from the target interval, and a signed polynomial gives its lower bound.
item.dc:creator: Scott D. Hughes

item.title: Kato-Milne cohomology over rational function fields in characteristic p>0
item.description: arXiv:2611.29511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let F be a field of characteristic p > 0. In this note, we describe the Kato-Milne cohomology of the rational function field F(x) in one variable x over F. In particular, we extend the Milnor-Scharlau exact sequence [12, Theorem 5.2] to characteristic p. As an application of this exact sequence, we further obtain the norm theorem [16, Theorem A.3] in characteristic p.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Laghribi, Trisha Maiti

item.title: A Goldbach-Type Problem for Random Multiplicative Functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.29521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the counts of the four sign patterns of a random multiplicative function on ordered decompositions $a+b=N$ into positive integers. The main term is $N/4$ in the nonvanishing model and $F(N)/4$ in the squarefree-supported model, where $F(N)$ counts the pairs with both summands squarefree and has asymptotic main term $\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{sf}}(N)N$. Let $\rho_q$ be the probability of a negative sign at the prime $q$. Set $m_q=\min(\rho_q,1-\rho_q)$, $A_N=\sum_{(\log N)^3<q\le N}m_q/q$, and $B(N)=\sum_{q\le N}m_q/q$. In the general model with independent prime vectors, almost surely for all sufficiently large integers $N$, the error for opposite-sign pairs is $O_{\mathcal X}(Ne^{-4A_N})$, and the error for same-sign pairs is $O_{\mathcal X}(N(e^{-4A_N}+e^{-2B(N)}))$. In four specified models, if the biases of the independent basic signs are square summable, then for every $\varepsilon>0$ the error is almost surely $O_{\varepsilon,\mathcal X}(N^{1/2+\varepsilon})$. In the completely multiplicative model under the same bias condition, we prove that $C_f(N)/\sqrt{N\log N}$ almost surely has limit superior $2$ and limit inferior $-2$. Together with a known bound for the one-point sum, this gives limit superior $1/2$ and limit inferior $-1/2$ for each normalized counting error about $N/4$
item.dc:creator: Tian Caolin

item.title: Rank-two twists of the Fermat cubic with $3$-primary Tate--Shafarevich group $(\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z})^{2m}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.29541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For each integer $m\ge0$ we construct infinitely many positive squarefree integers $k$ for which the Fermat cubic $E_k\colon x^3+y^3=k$ has Mordell--Weil rank two over $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\unicode{x0428}(E_k/\mathbb{Q})[3^\infty]\simeq(\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z})^{2m}$. Fixing $2m$ prime divisors of $k$ congruent to $-1$ modulo nine, with product $D$, we obtain $\gg_D X^{1/3}/(\log X)^6$ distinct parameters up to $X$. Two rational points on a $3$-isogenous curve come from the Stewart--Top sextic. Modulo their Kummer classes and a torsion class, the isogeny Selmer group has a basis given by the fixed primes. We realize every alternating matrix in this basis by prescribing the Frobenius classes of six primes in a fixed Galois extension. A nondegenerate matrix forces the rank to be exactly two and determines the entire primary group.
item.dc:creator: Hongfeng Wu, Li Zhu

item.title: Quadruples of integers whose elementary symmetric functions are perfect squares
item.description: arXiv:2611.29568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While Euler had considered the problem of finding three integers whose elementary symmetric functions are all squares, an extension of the problem to four integers has not been discussed in the mathematical literature till now. In this paper, we describe a method of generating infinitely many quadruples of positive integers whose elementary symmetric functions are all squares.
item.dc:creator: Ajai Choudhry

item.title: Certified $p$-adic normal forms: an Eliasson-Vey theorem and zero sets of orbits
item.description: arXiv:2611.29586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: I use the Smith form of the homological operator to construct partial Poincar\'e-Dulac normal forms near an equilibrium of a vector field on $\mathbb {Z}_p^d$ with coefficients divisible by $p$ (by $4$ if $p=2$). Retaining the directions whose removal would cost more than a fixed number of digits gives convergence on an explicit ball for any linear part. For polynomial fields, an exact integer check of the conjugacy defect certifies the computed flow to $K$ digits in rescaled coordinates. When the quadratic parts of an integrable Hamiltonian system at a rank-$0$ point span a Cartan subalgebra, the homological divisors in symplectic eigencoordinates are integers. This lets me use Newton iteration to obtain an exact $p$-adic Eliasson--Vey normal form at every prime and for every Williamson type. In exact linear normal coordinates, a polynomial restricted to an orbit gives a sum of exponentials, to which van der Poorten's bound of $2s-3$ zeros applies for a nonzero sum with $s\ge2$ distinct exponents. For integer orbits of polynomial maps, I combine exact modular orbits, Strassmann bounds and archimedean estimates in an adelic sieve. At every prime, increasing the modular depth eventually excludes a time class exactly when the interpolation along its center-manifold shadow has no zero in $\mathbb {Z}_p$.
item.dc:creator: Kirill Terskii

item.title: The Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer formula for CM elliptic curves of analytic rank one
item.description: arXiv:2611.29641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we prove the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer formula for elliptic curves over the field of rational numbers with complex multiplication and analytic rank one.
item.dc:creator: Xin Wan, Zerui Xiang, Ruichen Xu

item.title: Gowers-uniform sets with few arithmetic progressions
item.description: arXiv:2611.29676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For each fixed $s\geq 2$, we construct sparse sets $A\subset \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ such that the normalized indicator function $\nu_A$ of $A$ satisfies $\|\nu_A-1\|_{U^s}=o(1)$, while the number of three-term arithmetic progressions in $A$ is $o(|A|^3/N)$. This answers the counting form of a question of Gowers and Green, as formulated by Conlon, Fox and Zhao, on the pseudorandomness hypotheses needed in a relative Szemer\'{e}di theorem.
item.dc:creator: Xuancheng Shao

item.title: Two-term Rogers dilogarithm identities over cubic fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.29740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study normalized two-term Rogers dilogarithm relations in cubic fields. For integral, nonunimodular rank-two monomial configurations whose base argument generates a totally real cubic field, finite-prime valuations force the arguments and their complements to be units. Normalization preserves the generated order and reduces the problem to two cubic families without a maximal-order assumption. In the simplest cubic family, an existing unit-equation classification yields exactly ten relations up to simultaneous reflection, with distinct coefficients 2, 3, 7, 13, 19, 31 and 97. Explicit five-term certificates prove all ten evaluations. In the second family, a sharpened lower bound for the height of a solution, together with the two-logarithm theorem of Laurent, Mignotte and Nesterenko, reduces the unit equation to a short certified computation, and the family contributes no relation in this class. A unit-index argument restricts, independently, wedge relations between arbitrary exceptional units of non-Galois totally real cubic fields: any such relation would have a coefficient with no prime factor below 23 and would contradict Ennola's conjecture on fundamental units. In cubic fields with one real embedding, the only five-term certified relation between exceptional units with coefficient greater than one is Lewin's identity. Together, these results give exactly eleven identities in the two classes considered, up to the stated reflections.
item.dc:creator: Cetin Hakimoglu-Brown

item.title: Classes de Steinitz d'extensions galoisiennes non ramifi\'ees
item.description: arXiv:2611.29770v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K$ be a number field and $Cl_{K}$ its class group. Let $\Gamma$ be a finite group. We denote by $ R_{nr}(K,\Gamma)$ the subset of $Cl_{K}$ formed by the classes which are realizable as Steinitz classes of Galois extensions of $K$, unramified at the finite places of $K$ and having a Galois group isomorphic to $\Gamma$. If $\Gamma$ is abelian and the narrow class number of $K$ is prime to the order of $\Gamma$, then $R_{nr}(K,\Gamma)=\emptyset$. In the present article, for any $\Gamma$ we consider the set $R'_{nr}(K,\Gamma):=\lbrace 1 \rbrace \cup R_{nr}(K,\Gamma)$. We prove that $R'_{nr}(K, \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})$ is a subgroup of $Cl_{K,2}:=\lbrace c\in Cl_{K}\vert c^{2}=1\rbrace$ ; furthermore, it is equal to $Cl_{K,2}$ under a certain assumption on $K$. Using this result we show that $R'_{nr}(K,\Gamma)$ is a subgroup of $R'_{nr}(K, \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})$ if $\Gamma$ either has odd order, or has a noncyclic $2$-Sylow subgroup (for instance $\Gamma$ a nonabelian $2$-group, $\Gamma=S_n$ or $A_n$, with $n\geq 4$), or has a normal cyclic $2$-Sylow subgroup (for instance $\Gamma$ nilpotent having even order).
item.dc:creator: Ayoub Al Uartassi, Boucha\"ib Soda\"igui, Mohammed Taous

item.title: A linear bound in Waring's problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.29821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that $G(k) \asymp k$ in Waring's problem.
item.dc:creator: Sam Chow, Rainer Dietmann

item.title: Twisted K-Theory and Reduced Norms over Global and Higher Local Fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.29825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the Merkurjev--Suslin conjecture concerning reduced norms over both global and local fields. Furthermore, in both settings, we construct maps between truncated K-theory spectra that induce the reduced norms in degrees 1 and 2, and show that these maps are equivalences over local fields. Over global fields, we establish finiteness properties of their fibers and give a detailed description of their structure. We also extend the Merkurjev--Suslin conjecture to two-dimensional local fields and three-dimensional local fields with characteristic sequences (0, 0, 0) and (0, 0, p), and prove it in these settings. Finally, we apply these results to noncommutative class field theory over number fields and obtain a description of the Artin map associated with a central simple algebra.
item.dc:creator: Hisato Matsukawa

item.title: Orbital Integrals on Unitary Groups and Zeta Values
item.description: arXiv:2611.29994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We generalize Yun's interpolation formula for orbital integrals on $\mathrm{GL}_n$ in terms of Dedekind zeta functions to stable orbital integrals on unitary groups. Our approach combines Xiao's germ expansion of orbital integrals and the Jacquet-Rallis fundamental lemma.
item.dc:creator: Li Cai, Xuan Cui

item.title: A cyclic analogue of Schur multiple zeta values
item.description: arXiv:2611.30000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we introduce a cyclic analogue of Schur multiple zeta values. For a diagonally constant index on a periodically extended skew Young diagram, it is a sum over semi-standard cyclic Young tableaux. It includes the cyclic multiple zeta values of Hirose, Murahara and Murakami as a special case. The first two main results are a cyclic analogue of the Maesaka--Seki--Watanabe formula for truncated sums and an {integral--series identity} under an admissibility condition. As an application, we give a proof of $4^n\zeta(\{1,3\}^n)=\zeta(\{4\}^n)$ by counting linear extensions of a poset. The third main result expresses a cyclic Schur multiple harmonic sum as a finite signed sum of Schur multiple harmonic sums with the same number of boxes and the same multiset of exponents.
item.dc:creator: Ku-Yu Fan, Hau-Yi Lin, Jinbo Yu

item.title: Improvements to explicit Burgess-strength bounds for quadratic characters of prime modulus
item.description: arXiv:2611.30126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For positive integers $M$ and $N$, consider the character sum $S(M,N)=\sum_{n\in[M,M+N)}\chi_p(n)$, where $\chi_p$ is the quadratic character modulo $p$. Burgess proved that $S(M,N)\ll N^{1-1/r}p^{\frac{r+1}{4r^2}+\varepsilon}$ for any integer $r\geq 2$ and any real $\varepsilon>0$. This was made explicit by Booker, who showed (under size restrictions on $M$, $N$, $p$ and $r$) that $\lvert S(M,N)\rvert \leq \alpha(r)N^{1-1/r}p^{\frac{r+1}{4r^2}}(\beta(r)+\log{p})^{1/2r}$, where $\alpha(r)$ and $\beta(r)$ are given in (Booker, 2006). We show that when $M$ is not too small compared to $N$, we can improve $\beta(r)$ by a fixed amount. If $M$ is also not too large compared to $N$, we can further improve $\beta(r)$ by an amount proportional to $\frac{M}{M+N}$.
item.dc:creator: James Punch

item.title: The Riemann Hypothesis for L-Functions of Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families: Frobenius Polynomials and Intersection Cohomology
item.description: arXiv:2611.30138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Frobenius polynomials attached to linearly constrained Kloosterman families, taking the rank-$r(n)=2^n-\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, weight-$(n+1)$ sheaf of the author's companion papers as an explicit input. The present contribution is the passage from that sheaf to local characteristic polynomials and the intermediate-extension intersection cohomology on $(\mathbb P^1)^n$. We prove the local reciprocal-root bounds and the degreewise purity of the completed factors; their weights are $n+1+i$ in cohomological degree $i$. Using the imported arithmetic relative-image identification, we construct a reflection pairing and derive the completed functional equation with positive root number. We also give a canonical Frobenius-equivariant splitting of the fibrewise compact-support/parabolic sequence by separation of weights and examine the comparison on open coordinate-zero divisors. The statements do not assume global arithmetic Frobenius semisimplicity or a higher-codimension wild-boundary exchange. An explicit source-and-dependency ledger distinguishes results imported from the companion papers from deductions established here.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Ebadi

item.title: Endomorphism algebras of Drinfeld modules in special characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2611.30299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify the division algebras that occur as endomorphism algebras of Drinfeld modules of a given rank in special characteristic which cannot be defined over a finite field. The classification is in terms of the center of the algebra and its local invariants. Together with the known results in generic characteristic and over finite fields, this gives a complete description of the endomorphism algebras of Drinfeld modules of a given rank.
item.dc:creator: Mihran Papikian

item.title: Signed Admissible Regions and 2-adic Area Obstructions for Perfect Triangles
item.description: arXiv:2611.30430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A perfect triangle is a triangle whose sides, medians and area are all integers; whether one exists is an open problem. We study Buchholz's rational parametrization of triangles with two rational medians on the whole $(\theta,\phi)$-plane, allowing the generated side lengths to be negative. We factor its Heron polynomial $H(\theta,\phi)$ into ten explicit factors and show that the points whose componentwise absolute values form a triangle are exactly those with $H>0$; the points giving positive side lengths directly form three open quadrilaterals, one of which is the region used by Buchholz and Rathbun. Every triangle with two rational medians arises from sixteen signed parameter points, given by explicit rational functions. Rational area forces $H$ to be a square in $\mathbb{Q}_2$, and the valuation and the unit part of $H$ yield parity and modulo-8 conditions in three valuation ranges. Since a triangle is excluded as soon as one of its sixteen parameter points fails a test, these conditions exclude infinite families of signed admissible parameters, including non-integral ones. The conditions are necessary only and do not settle the existence of perfect triangles.
item.dc:creator: Qizhen Wang

item.title: Bilinear sum involving $GL(3)$ Fourier coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.30547v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we use the circle method to establish non-trivial bounds for certain summatory functions and a bilinear sum involving the Fourier coefficients of a general Hecke-Maass cusp form on $SL(3,\mathbb{Z})$.
item.dc:creator: Mohd Harun, Saurabh Kumar Singh

item.title: Connected descent and Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles
item.description: arXiv:2611.30562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We answer a question by Hui Zhang and show that, for any smooth, quasi-projective, geometrically integral variety X over a number field k, the connected descent set for 0-cycles is equal to the Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles. In particular, the connected descent and the abelianised connected descent sets for 0-cycles coincide. In the same spirit, we also show that the descent set under all tori for 0-cycles is equal to the algebraic Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles. Finally, we give a new formulation of Conjecture (E) using the connected descent sets.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Balestrieri

item.title: Wirsing type approximation over totally real and totally $p$-adic extensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.30585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish Wirsing-type bounds for approximation of real and $p$-adic transcendental numbers by totally real and totally $p$-adic algebraic numbers, respectively. More precisely, for every $n\ge 1$, we show that every transcendental $\xi\in\mathbb{Q}_p$ admits infinitely many totally $p$-adic algebraic approximants $\alpha$ of degree at most $n$ satisfying $0<|\xi-\alpha|_p\ll H(\alpha)^{-1-\lceil n/2\rceil}$. We improve this bound for even $n\ge 4$. For each $n\geq 2$, we also show that every real number $\xi$ that is not algebraic of degree at most $n$ admits totally real approximants of degree at most $n$ with a bound stronger than Wirsing's. In both cases, we can also restrict the approximants to be totally $\ell$-adic for every prime $\ell$ in a fixed finite set.
item.dc:creator: Anup B. Dixit, Hitesh Kumar

item.title: Quantum Variance of Holomorphic Modular Forms and Benjamini-Schramm Convergence
item.description: arXiv:2611.30628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study quantum variance for holomorphic modular forms of fixed weight on sequences of compact hyperbolic surfaces converging to the hyperbolic plane in the sense of Benjamini-Schramm. We first show that quantum ergodicity need not hold for an arbitrary choice of orthonormal basis, even for sequences with a uniform lower bound on the injectivity radius and a uniform spectral gap. The counterexample is constructed using a tower of coverings and arises from the identity contribution in the automorphic kernel. We then show that this obstruction is exceptional from the point of view of the choice of basis. For a Haar random orthonormal basis of holomorphic modular forms, the quantum variance converges to zero with probability tending to one uniformly over all observables with bounded supremum norm. The proof combines estimates for the Hilbert-Schmidt norm of a projected multiplication operator with the Haar expectation of the quantum variance, concentration of measure on the special unitary group and a finite-dimensional approximation of the space of observables.
item.dc:creator: Kemin Qiu

item.title: On the work of Jacob Tsimerman
item.description: arXiv:2611.30644v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Jacob Tsimerman was awarded a Fields Medal at the\ ICM in Philadelphia on July 23, 2026 ``For his contribution in the recasting of o-minimality as a fundamental method of arithmetic and complex algebraic geometry, and his role in the proof of many central conjectures including Griffiths' conjecture on the algebraicity of images of the period maps, and the Andr\'e-Oort conjecture for Siegel modular varieties.'' We describe this work.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Pila

item.title: Arithmetic Winding Curves in $\mathbb{F}_1$ Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.30682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct arithmetic winding curves from cyclic covers and the completions of a number field $K$. Transfers between cyclic periods give the primitive cyclotomic relations. Selected factors of the equivariant endomorphism rings of their derived intersections are finite fields in odd residue characteristic and length-two Witt rings in residue characteristic two. Valuation covers carry these periods on the curve $Y_K$. Their normal coordinates realize deck shifts as Schwartz operators in Meyer's arithmetic trace formula, and their puncture differentials give the finite Euler factors of $\zeta_K$. We construct a sheaf on $Y_K$ for which the middle Fourier--Poisson representation embeds as a $C_K$-module in ordinary first sheaf cohomology. The Dedekind-zeta component is an equivariant direct summand. The injection uses valuation monodromy at the finite places and adelic Poisson summation on the archimedean charts. The cup product of two image classes vanishes with tensor-product coefficients, also after conjugating one factor. On the section side, tensor degree and integral jets give multiplicative lattices, explicit duality quotients, and relative theta identities. A principal cyclotomic twist with determinant one on truncated jets yields a quadratic lower bound for the logarithmic index in a family of increasing rank. The fixed-weight Poisson quotients preserve finite collections of Mellin derivatives at Hecke zeros of orders below their respective multiplicities.
item.dc:creator: SeungJu Lee

item.title: Statistics of Fundamental Fourier Coefficients of Cusp Forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.30687v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study sign changes of Fourier coefficients of elliptic and Siegel modular forms in considerable generality. For any $N \geq 1$ and an arbitrary non-zero elliptic cusp form $f\in S_\kappa (\Gamma_1(N))$ ($\kappa \in \frac{1}{2} \mathbb{Z}$) with real Fourier coefficients, we show that a positive proportion of its non-zero Fourier coefficients change sign if $\kappa \geq 1$ is integral. If $\kappa \geq 1/2$ is half-integral, we get an almost optimal result. As applications, we establish quantitative sign-change results for `fundamental' Fourier coefficients of Siegel cusp forms of arbitrary degree $n$. These improve the previous best known results on the number of non-zero fundamental Fourier coefficients, even in degree $n=1$.
item.dc:creator: Soumya Das, Animesh Sarkar

item.title: Notes on an elementary proof of Weil II from Hexagon
item.description: arXiv:2611.30749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, L. Alp\"oge sketched an elementary proof of Deligne's weight bound in footnote 3 of his remark on joint work with Claude on the Riemann hypothesis. An expanded, AI-generated account appeared on Hexagon, where it was posted by F. Alderliefste. This note gives an exposition of the proof presented there.
item.dc:creator: Dingxin Zhang

item.title: Distribution of Rademacher random multiplicative functions in short intervals, with proper normalization
item.description: arXiv:2611.30763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the limiting distribution of partial sums $\sum_{x<n\le x+y}f(n)$ of a Rademacher random multiplicative function over short intervals. Combined with the theorem of Soundararajan and Xu, our result gives a standard real Gaussian limit, with a suitable deterministic normalization, throughout $x^{1/5}\log x\ll y=o(x)$. This resolves the Rademacher extension raised by Harper, Soundararajan and Xu. The normalization is smaller than the standard deviation by a factor tending to zero when $\log(x/y)=o(\sqrt{\log\log x})$. As an application of our method, we also obtain a complex Gaussian limit for short interval sums twisted by a fixed primitive nonreal Dirichlet character.
item.dc:creator: Renjie Zhu, Tianping Zhang

item.title: Irreducibility of Primitive Special Cycles in Locally Symmetric Spaces of Orthogonal Type
item.description: arXiv:2611.30782v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $L$ be an even lattice of signature $(n_1,n_2)$ with $n_1\geq k+1,n_2\geq 2$ and let $X$ denote the quotient of the symmetric space associated to $O(L\otimes_\mathbb{Z}\mathbb{R})$ by the discriminant kernel of positive spinor norm. We show that primitive special cycles in $X$ of real codimension at most $kn_2$ are irreducible if $L$ splits off $k+1$ hyperbolic planes locally at every prime.
item.dc:creator: Niklas Ludwig

item.title: Linear forms in logarithms of rational numbers: an ineffective measure with the best possible exponent
item.description: arXiv:2611.30820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $a_1,\dots,a_n$ be positive rational numbers without a nontrivial multiplicative relation. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a constant $C>0$, not effective, such that $|h_0+h_1\log a_1+\dots+h_n\log a_n| \ge C\max(1,|h_0|,\dots,|h_n|)^{-n-\varepsilon}$ for all integers $h_0,\dots,h_n$, not all zero. The exponent $n$ is best possible. For $n=1$ this is the known fact that the irrationality exponent of $\log a$ is $2$; for $h_0=0$ it gives the exponent $n$ for the linear forms $h_1\log a_1+\dots+h_n\log a_n$. The proof is an induction on $n$, starting from $n=1$. The step from $n-1$ to $n$ logarithms uses an interpolation determinant on $\mathbb{G}_m^n\times\mathbb{G}_a$ at the multiples of a rational point, in the manner of arXiv:2610.28079; its geometric part, a curve inequality, is proved by a second induction, on the number of torus coordinates, with the two-torus inequality of arXiv:2610.28079 as the base. The method is the interpolation and determinant method of OpenAI's preprint on the irrationality exponent of $\pi$; the case $n=1$ was obtained earlier by Liu, Jiang and Zhang (arXiv:2610.10192). The theorem and its corollary are verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib; the sources are in the ancillary files, on top of the Lean supplement of arXiv:2610.28079. This paper follows the formal proof: every definition, constant and intermediate statement is given in the form in which it is formalized, with the name of the Lean declaration.
item.dc:creator: Gregory V. Chudnovsky

item.title: Exact Hausdorff and Packing Dimensions of $k$-Singular Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.30847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the Hausdorff and packing dimensions of $k$-singular $m\times n$ matrices for all $m,n\geq1$ and $2\leq k\leq m+n-1$. Such matrices are characterized by the $(k-1)$st successive minimum tending to zero and the $(k+1)$st tending to infinity along an associated diagonal-flow orbit. The exact formula was announced by Das--Fishman--Simmons--Urba\'nski in 2017 and formulated as a conjecture in their 2024 paper, which proves the matching Hausdorff-dimension lower bound. We prove the matching packing-dimension upper bound, resolving their Conjecture~5.1. The proof uses their variational principle together with a linear potential that corrects the local contraction rate. The corrected rate is nondecreasing under mergers of adjacent equality blocks that preserve a separating gap, reducing the estimate to two-block configurations. Secant-line estimates at integer points then allow us to choose a single pair of potential coefficients that controls both possible separating gaps. The dimension formula remains valid after excluding trivially singular matrices.
item.dc:creator: Shahriar Mirzadeh

item.title: Hypergeometric Abelian Surfaces and Triangle-Group Levels
item.description: arXiv:2611.30864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study three families of hypergeometric abelian surfaces with real multiplication by $K=\Q(\sqrt5)$. We determine their integral homology lattices and monodromy, including the choice of lattice at the ramified prime above $5$ in the plus family. One family is isomorphic to an explicit quadratic twist of a genus-two Frey Jacobian, with the two real-multiplication embeddings exchanged. The specified isogeny is twice an isomorphism and has kernel equal to the full $2$-torsion. Each family gives two real rank-two representations, with projective local monodromies of order $5$ at two punctures and parabolic monodromy at the third. Exactly one of the six projective representations is discrete, with image $\Delta(5,5,\infty)$. Reduction at the two primes above $11$ gives six degree-$12$, genus-two covers parametrizing torsion lines. For the family with a discrete constituent, these Borel covers are the triangular modular curves $X_0(5,5,\infty;\mathfrak q)$; the comparison descends to ordered covers over $K$. The generic arithmetic projective image is $\PGL_2(\F_{11})$; the Galois closure of each Borel cover has constant field $K(\sqrt{-11})$.
item.dc:creator: Devendra Tiwari

item.title: The Exact Value of the Rankin Number gamma_{5,2}
item.description: arXiv:2611.30885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Rankin number gamma_{5,2} measures the exact upper bound for the squared determinant of the densest 2-dimensional sublattice of any 5-dimensional lattice of determinant one. We prove that gamma_{5,2}=16^{1/5}, attained by D*_5.
item.dc:creator: Zhixing Li

item.title: The optimal exponent in the Erd\H{o}s--Fuchs theorem for $k$-fold sums
item.description: arXiv:2611.30890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k\ge 2$ be an integer. For an infinite set $A$ of nonnegative integers and a real number $x\ge0$, let $r_k(A,x)$ be the number of $k$-tuples $(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\in A^k$ satisfying $a_1+\cdots +a_k\le x$. In this paper, we prove that $r_k(A,x)=cx+o(x^{(1-1/k)^2})$ is impossible for any real number $c>0$. The exponent $(1-1/k)^2$ is best possible for $k\ge3$ by a recent result of Guo and Yan. Moreover, we obtain a mean-square estimate of $r_k(A,x)-cx$ and confirm a conjecture of Chen and Tang for every $k\ge3$.
item.dc:creator: Xiao-Hui Yan

item.title: A Classification of Low Genus Modular Curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.30908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be an open subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}})$ satisfying $\det(G)=\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}^{\times}$ and $-I\in G$. Associated to $G$, there is a modular curve $X_G$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$ which parametrizes elliptic curves with $G$-level structure. We give a classification of modular curves with genus equal to a fixed nonnegative integer $g$. In particular, we show that all modular curves of genus $g$ lie in finitely many families of $\mathbb{Q}^{\mathrm{ab}}$-twists of modular curves. We also describe an algorithm for computing all families of modular curves of a fixed genus $g$ and use this to compute projective models for these modular curves. This algorithm has been fully implemented for $g \leq 12$. In an appendix with Yongyuan Huang and Rakvi, we describe two algorithms, one for computing rational functions on modular curves given as quotients of two modular forms of the same weight, and the other for computing models for the generic fibers of universal elliptic curves $\mathcal{E}_G$, where $G\subset \mathrm{GL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}})$ is an open subgroup satisfying $\det(G)=\widehat{\mathbb{Z}}^{\times}$ and $-I\notin G$.
item.dc:creator: Eray Karabiyik

item.title: Unified Schur multiple zeta functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.30949v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define symmetric multiple zeta values, unified zeta functions, and finite zeta values in the Schur setting. We establish a Jacobi--Trudi formula and a Giambelli formula for unified Schur multiple zeta functions, and we show that there is a one-to-one correspondence between finite and symmetric Schur multiple zeta values under the Kaneko--Zagier conjecture. We also show a vanishing property for a symmetric sum of finite Schur multiple zeta values, generalizing a result obtained by Hoffman for finite multiple zeta values.
item.dc:creator: Nako Kamiyama, Simon Rutard

item.title: Three commuting matrices whose lifts never commute
item.description: arXiv:2611.30952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct pairwise commuting matrices over $\mathbb{F}_p$ which have no pairwise commuting lifts to $\mathbb{Z}/p^2\mathbb{Z}$. Equivalently, there are mod $p$ representations of the absolute Galois group of the field of iterated Laurent series $\mathbb{C}((x_1))\cdots((x_d))$ which do not lift modulo $p^2$.
item.dc:creator: Charles De Clercq

item.title: Modularity of Heegner Cycles and Arithmetic Inner Products on Kuga-Sato Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.31153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For \(\kappa\ge2\), the principal part of a weakly holomorphic modular form of weight \(\tfrac32-\kappa\) determines a linear combination of codimension-\(\kappa\) Heegner cycles on a compact Kuga--Sato variety. We use isogeny correspondences to prove that every such combination vanishes in the Chow group with complex coefficients. These rational equivalences imply that the generating series of Heegner cycles is a Chow-valued cusp form of weight \(\kappa+\tfrac12\) at every level and for every compatible fundamental twist. We prove an arithmetic inner product formula for theta lifts on the modular curve \(X_0(N)\) and on higher-dimensional Kuga--Sato varieties. It expresses their height pairings in terms of central derivatives of quadratic twists of newform \(L\)-functions, with an explicit product of local operators on oldspaces. On each primitive newform line selected by the twist, the height of one projected Heegner cycle at a fundamental index with nonzero Fourier coefficient determines all pairings of projected cycles on that line. This specialization recovers the Gross--Zagier formula in weight two and the genus-character case of the Gross--Zagier--Zhang formula in higher weight.
item.dc:creator: Tuoping Du

item.title: Toward a Classification of Differentially $3$-Uniform Power Mappings over $\F_{p^2}$ and $\F_{p^3}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.31199v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the classification, up to the CCZ-equivalence, of differentially $3$-uniform power mappings over quadratic and cubic extensions of prime fields. Over $\F_{p^2}$ exhaustive searches for primes $3<p<300$ found only the known families E1 and E4 for $p>23$. Over $\F_{p^3}$, the previously unexplained exponents for $7<p<200$ belong to a single family. We give an elementary proof that this family has differential uniformity at most $3$ for primes $p\equiv 3 \pmod 4$, and prove that the bound is attained for $p>1444$.
item.dc:creator: Mohit Pal

item.title: Diophantine sets over global function fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.31218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $q\equiv 3\bmod 4$ be a prime power and let $K$ be a finite separable extension of the field of rational functions $\mathbb F_q(t)$, with constant field $\mathbb F_q$. We show that $\mathbb F_q[t]$ is Diophantine in $\mathbb F_q(t)$ and that the latter is Diophantine in $K$. We deduce from work of Demeyer that $K$ has the DPRM property: Diophantine sets over $K$ are the same as listable sets.
item.dc:creator: Hector Pasten, Xavier Vidaux

item.title: Lattices of Minimal Covolume in $\mathrm{SL}_2$ over Dyadic Local Fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.28453v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we determine the minimal covolume among lattices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ for each finite extension $K/\mathbb{Q}_2$. Using the action of $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ on its Bruhat--Tits tree, we investigate the shape of the fixed subtrees of finite subgroups, particularly cyclic and dicyclic subgroups of $2$-power order. We determine which larger vertex stabilizers can occur at boundary vertices of the fixed subtrees of dicyclic subgroups and subgroups isomorphic to $2.A_4$. We use these results to construct graphs of groups defining lattices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(K)$ and prove that these lattices attain the minimal covolume. This extends a result of Lubotzky and Weigel, which treats finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ for odd primes $p$.
item.dc:creator: Yukun Du

item.title: On the tensor product of semistable Hermitian adelic vector bundles over an adelic curve
item.description: arXiv:2611.28474v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove tensor semistability for Hermitian adelic vector bundles on proper adelic curves whose underlying fields are countable and of characteristic zero. The central estimate concerns the canonical integral Specht lattice of a rectangular partition with fixed height: its logarithmic covolume, divided by its rank and tensor degree, tends to zero. We prove this estimate from monic seminormal norms and an exact hypergeometric law weighted by the square of a Vandermonde product for tableau prefixes. Constant adelic Specht bundles and equivariant contractions then yield the slope inequality for every geometrically semistable subspace of a finite tensor product. The correction is the measure of the Archimedean places times a sublinear Specht term and vanishes in the limit as the auxiliary degree tends to infinity. An instability-filtration argument completes the reduction to arbitrary factors and identifies the tensor product Harder--Narasimhan filtration. The number field specialization gives the Bost tensor semistability conjecture in all ranks.
item.dc:creator: Huayi Chen, Yijun Yuan

item.title: The local lifting conjecture for dihedral groups of order $2p^n$
item.description: arXiv:2611.29297v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic $p$, and let $D_{p^n}$ denote the dihedral group of order $2p^n$. A local $D_{p^n}$-action is a faithful action of $D_{p^n}$ on the formal power series ring $k[[z]]$ by continuous $k$-automorphisms. The strong Oort conjecture of Chinburg, Guralnick and Harbater predicts that every such action lifts to characteristic zero. This is also the dihedral case of the local lifting conjecture of Obus. We prove this assertion for $n=2$ and every odd prime $p$. More precisely, given a local $D_{p^2}$-action on $k[[z]]$, we construct an action on $R[[Z]]$ by $R$-automorphisms whose reduction modulo the maximal ideal of $R$ is the given action, where $R$ is a complete discrete valuation ring finite over the Witt ring $W(k)$. For arbitrary $n$, let $C_{p^n}$ be the cyclic subgroup of index two in $D_{p^n}$, and let $u_1,\ldots,u_n$ be the upper ramification jumps of $k((z))/k((z))^{C_{p^n}}$. We prove that the action lifts if $u_i\equiv-1\pmod{2p}$ for every $i$. When $p=3$, we also prove lifting under the hypotheses $u_i\equiv5\pmod6$ for $2\leq i<n$ and $3\nmid u_n$.
item.dc:creator: Jayashree Kalita, Anwesh Ray

item.title: Contiguous relations for elliptic analogues of partial sums of very-well-poised ${}_8\psi_8$ series
item.description: arXiv:2611.29300v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce finite elliptic analogues of partial sums of a balanced very-well-poised ${}_8\psi_8$ series. By combining Abel's lemma on summation by parts with the Riemann theta relation, we establish two contiguous relations. Iterating the second relation gives two finite transformation formulas.
item.dc:creator: Takumi Maesaka

item.title: Optimal odd unimodular lattices in dimensions $49$ through $59$
item.description: arXiv:2611.29304v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is shown that the largest minimum norm among unimodular lattices is $4$ in dimension $49$ and $5$ in dimensions $50$, $51$, $57$ and $58$. We also study the theta series of optimal unimodular lattices in every dimension from $49$ through $59$. In dimensions $50$, $51$ and $57$, the first known examples of unimodular lattices with minimum norm $5$ are obtained from self-dual codes by Construction~A. There exist at least $25$, $2$, $3$, $7$ and $12$ nonisomorphic optimal unimodular lattices in dimensions $49$, $55$, $57$, $58$ and $59$, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Masaaki Harada

item.title: Subshifts of finite type and parameter density for intermediate \(-\beta\)-transformations
item.description: arXiv:2611.29611v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the subshifts \(\Omega_{-\beta,\alpha}\) associated with the intermediate \(-\beta\)-transformations \(x\mapsto-\beta x+\alpha\pmod1\), where \((\beta,\alpha)\in\Delta_-:=\{(b,a):1<b<2,\ b-1<a<1\}\). We prove that $\Omega_{-\beta,\alpha}$ is of finite type if and only if both endpoints of \([0,1]\) reach the discontinuity \(c_{\beta,\alpha}=\alpha/\beta\). We also prove that the set of parameters \((\beta,\alpha)\) for which \(\Omega_{-\beta,\alpha}\) is a subshift of finite type is dense in \(\Delta_-\). The approximating parameters can be chosen so that both kneading invariants converge to those of the original map.
item.dc:creator: Yiming Ding, Yun Sun

item.title: Universal Implications Among $k$-Prime Graph Labelings
item.description: arXiv:2611.29669v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $k\ge1$, let $\mathcal P_k$ be the class of graphs admitting a bijective labeling by consecutive integers beginning at $k$, with coprime labels at adjacent vertices. We determine all universal inclusions between distinct such classes: $\mathcal P_i\subseteq\mathcal P_j$ holds for $i\ne j$ if and only if $(i,j)=(2,1)$ or $(3,1)$. In particular, the classes are pairwise distinct. The proof translates universal inclusion into a spanning-embedding question for coprimality graphs on consecutive integer intervals. Edge-count identities, arithmetic-progression estimates, and prime-residue switching exclude all other inclusions; a prime-gap argument reduces the remaining finite range to fifteen explicit rational inequalities. We further show that, for each nonexceptional ordered pair, the graph orders at which edge counts obstruct inclusion have a positive natural density. This density is described through a limiting distribution of correlated Euler products, for which we give an atomlessness argument. The classification resolves the distinct-index formulation of the universal-implication conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Jing Zhang, Yuan Li

item.title: Grothendieck--Serre for quasi-split groups over two-dimensional regular local rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.29864v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the Grothendieck--Serre conjecture for quasi-split reductive group schemes over two-dimensional regular local rings, that is, every generically trivial torsor under a quasi-split group scheme $G$ over a regular local ring $R$ of dimension two is trivial. Our main result is new when $R$ is ramified and generalizes Nisnevich's result by removing the assumption that the residue field is infinite. By formal patching of torsors and valuative criteria, we are reduced to showing a product formula when $G$ is semisimple and simply connected. Then, we take advantage of relative simple reflections and relative Bruhat decomposition to prove a generation by rank-one subgroups. The analysis on Dynkin diagrams with Galois actions reduces us to $\operatorname{SL}_2$ and three-dimensional $\operatorname{SU}$ factors. For the special unitary case, we treat Hermitian forms by using stabilizations and cancellation to finish the proof.
item.dc:creator: Ning Guo

item.title: Parking Functions inspired by board games
item.description: arXiv:2611.29890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce two new parking schemes inspired by the classic board games Monopoly and backgammon. We consider a one-way street with $n$ parking spots and a queue of $n$ cars waiting to park. Each car has a preferred parking spot and enters in sequence to park. Under the Monopoly parking scheme, if a car finds its preferred spot occupied, it returns to the start of the street and parks in the first available spot it encounters. Under the backgammon parking scheme, if a car finds its preferred spot occupied, it bumps the already parked car out of that spot and takes its place. The bumped car then returns to the start of the street and parks in the first available spot it encounters. A preference list is a parking function for a given parking scheme if all cars successfully park under that scheme. We prove that all preference lists are parking functions under both the Monopoly and backgammon parking schemes. However, the final parking order differs significantly between the two schemes. For a fixed permutation $\pi$, we provide a product formula for the number of Monopoly parking functions resulting in the outcome $\pi$. Analogously, we show that the number of backgammon parking functions with outcome $\pi$ is bounded below by $2^{n-1}$ and bounded above by the $n$-th Catalan number. We also obtain exact formulas involving Motzkin numbers for several families of outcomes. We define the displacement of a car as the absolute difference between the spot where a car ultimately parks and its preferred spot. Displacement multisets encode the displacements for cars with nonzero displacement. We provide formulas for the number of backgammon parking functions with a fixed displacement multiset of cardinality at most $2$, as well as for the number of Monopoly parking functions whose displacement multiset is a given singleton set. We conclude with some directions for further research.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Clifton, Pamela E. Harris, Maryam Khaqan

item.title: Rank-Two Attractors and Modularity for a Mirror Bicubic
item.description: arXiv:2611.30234v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the mirror family $\mathcal X_\lambda$ of the bicubic Calabi-Yau threefold, obtained from a family of complete intersections of two cubics in $\mathbb P^5$. We show that the four-dimensional weight-three Hodge structure of the fibers over $\lambda^6 = -8$ splits into two rational rank-two pieces of Hodge types $(1,0,0,1)$ and $(0,1,1,0)$; in particular, these points are rank-two attractor points. Using a Hesse pencil fiber-product realization, equivariant point counting, and the Serre-Faltings-Livne method, we identify their semisimplified $\ell$-adic Galois representations with those attached to the weight-four newform $f_{\mathsf{54.4.a.c}}$ and the Tate twist of the weight-two newform $f_{\mathsf{54.2.a.a}}$, where these labels refer to the L-functions and modular forms database.
item.dc:creator: Yibing Chen, Emanuel Scheidegger

item.title: The Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.30237v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the Tate conjecture for non-CM and non-ordinary abelian fourfolds over positive characteristic function fields. Combining our previous works (2512.00687 and 2608.28651), this establishes the Tate conjecture for abelian fourfolds over finitely generated fields. Along the way, we classify the $l$-adic monodromy of abelian fourfolds in characteristic $p$ via mixed characteristic lifts and methods from convergent and overconvergent crystalline monodromy, and show that Zarhin's minuscule weights conjecture holds for abelian varieties up to dimension 4. These enable us to prove a characteristic $p$ variant of the Mumford--Tate conjecture for most abelian fourfolds, and reduce the Tate conjecture to Markman's results on the Hodge conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Matt Broe, Ruofan Jiang

item.title: Quasi-abelian Cousin groups of number fields:a Galois-orbit criterion and the complete list
item.description: arXiv:2611.30386v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let K be a number field with at least one complex place. A choice S of one embedding K $\rightarrow$ C at each place embeds the ring of integers of K as a discrete subgroup of Cn, where n is the number of places of K. The quotient T\_K,S is a Cousin group, or a complex torus if K is totally imaginary. We determine exactly when T\_K,S is quasi-abelian. The answer is a Galois criterion: no complex conjugation of the Galois closure of K may interchange two of the chosen complex embeddings. Equivalently, S is lifted from a subfield with at most one complex place above each place of the largest totally real subfield of K. For totally imaginary K this is the theorem of Shimura and Taniyama on abelian varieties with complex multiplication; our results extend it to all number fields. We also obtain the rank of the N{\'e}ron--Severi group, and show that T\_K,S is either quasi-abelian or has only constant meromorphic functions.
item.dc:creator: Karl Oeljeklaus (AMU, I2M)

item.title: Degree three unramified cohomology of homogeneous spaces with finite stabilisers
item.description: arXiv:2611.31042v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We provide an explicit formula for the third unramified cohomology group of homogeneous spaces of $\mathrm{SL}_n$ with finite stabilisers and a rational point, valid over an arbitrary field of characteristic prime to the order of the stabilisers. As a concrete application, we compute this group explicitly for every generalised quaternion group over an arbitrary field of characteristic 0, and settle Noether's problem over the rational numbers in the negative for those of order at least 16, thereby generalising a classical result of Serre. Over an algebraically closed field, our formula recovers and sharpens a theorem of Peyre; we further show that universal triviality of unramified cohomology in degree at most three is equivalent to its vanishing in the same degrees. Over the function field of a $p$-adic curve, we extend a result of Harari-Scheiderer-Szamuely. Over a finite field, the formula is effective and yields an algorithm for computing the group explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Lagarde

item.title: $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic intersections of $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds with perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.31104v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that transverse intersections between smooth $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds in $\mathbb{C}_p^n$ and perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces of complementary $\mathbb{C}_p$-dimension are $n$-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic manifolds. In the case of the Banach--Colmez space $\mathrm{BC}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$, this is a strong form of the relativistic $p$-adic sunscreen conjecture. These results hold more generally with $\mathbb{C}_p$ replaced by an arbitrary complete algebraically closed extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and we also establish some non-linear analogs for infinite level Lubin--Tate spaces.
item.dc:creator: Sean Howe, Ray Li

item.title: A Quantum Model from the Riemann-Siegel Formula
item.description: arXiv:2611.31116v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a two-component quantum model in which destructive interference selects the critical-line zeros of a regularized zeta function within a continuous spectrum. Starting from the exact Riemann--Siegel integral representation, we define $\zeta_{\rm reg}(s)$ by subtracting the contribution of the pole at the origin. The two remaining contour integrals supply the interfering amplitudes. A Dirichlet heat filter suppresses high spatial frequencies, and an arithmetic dressing has a profile generated by prime-power dilations. These transformations map the dilation generator to a self-adjoint, parity--time ($PT$) symmetric Hamiltonian on a physical Hilbert space with a positive metric. Its spectrum is real and continuous. The computed lower critical-line zeros of $\zeta_{\rm reg}(s)$ lie close to the corresponding Riemann zeros and exhibit spacing and pair-correlation statistics consistent with the Gaussian unitary ensemble over the sampled range. Whether every analytic zero in the lower half of the critical strip belongs to the physical spectral family remains open.
item.dc:creator: Germ\'an Sierra

item.title: On Some Diophantine Parameters of the Cyclic Torsion Subgroups of Odd Order of Elliptic Curves over $\mathbb{Q}$
item.description: arXiv:0803.0058v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For elliptic curves $ E $ over the rational number field $ \Q, $ based on Mazur's classical result, we give in this paper some explicit Diophantine parameters for their cyclic torsion subgroups $ E(\Q)_{\text{tors}} $ of odd order. This work is a continuation of the ones in ([Q1], [QZ1$\sim $2]). Such explicit form of parameters might be useful in calculating torsion subgroups of elliptic curves over higher degree number fields.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: JP Journal of Algebra, Number Theory and Applications 65(6) (2026), 1001-1018
item.dc:creator: Derong Qiu

item.title: Cohomology of SL(3,Z) with coefficients in the standard representation
item.description: arXiv:2207.12276v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is a natural continuation of a joint paper with Bajpai, Harder and Moya Giusti \cite{BHHM}, even though it began as an answer to Goncharov's question. It that paper, we had complete description for all representations except for odd symmetric powers and their dual ones. For those representations we were left with two options: certain one dimensional module is a ghost space or not. Here we find the $H^2(SL_3(\Z),V_3)$ has ghost classes. It means that it is generated by a class from the cohomology of the Borel subgroup. With the techniques developed here, we show that the $d_2$ map of the spectral sequence for the boundary cohomology of $GL_4(\Z)$ is non-trivial if and only if there is a ghost class in $GL_3(\Z)$ (see Propositions 11 and 12.) We use a result of Elbaz-Vincent, Gangl and Soule to show that a spectral sequence related to $GL_4(\Z)$ does not degenerate at $E_2$-level. Then $d_2$ is non-trivial. Therefore, we obtain that $H^2(SL_3(\Z),V_3))$ is a ghost space, where $V_3$ is the standard representation.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Horozov

item.title: Functional equation, upper bounds and analogue of Lindel\"of hypothesis for the Barnes double zeta function
item.description: arXiv:2208.10786v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The functional equations of the Riemann zeta function, the Hurwitz zeta function, and the Lerch zeta function have been well known for a long time, and there is great importance in studying these zeta functions. For example, fundamental properties such as the upper bounds, the distribution of zeros, and the zero-free regions in the Riemann zeta function derive from functional equations. In this paper, we consider the functional equations for the Barnes double zeta-function $ \zeta_2 (s, \alpha ; v, w ) = \sum_{m=0}^\infty \sum_{n=0}^\infty (\alpha+vm+wn)^{-s} $. Additionally, by applying this functional equation and the Phragm\'en-Lindel\"of convexity principle, we obtain some upper bounds for $ \zeta_2(\sigma + it, \alpha ; v, w) $ with respect to $ t $ as $ t \rightarrow \infty $. Furthermore, we prove that an analogue of the Lindel"of hypothesis for the Barnes double zeta-function is equivalent to suitable upper bounds for its positive even moments on vertical lines in the critical strip.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Ramanujan mathematical Society, Vol. 41, No. 4 (2006), pp. 311-324
item.dc:creator: Takashi Miyagawa

item.title: The pro-$\mathcal{C}$ anabelian geometry of number fields
item.description: arXiv:2303.02931v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a number field and $\mathcal{C}$ a nontrivial full class of finite groups. Write $K^{\mathcal{C}}/K$ for the maximal pro-$\mathcal{C}$ Galois extension of $K$ and $G_K^{\mathcal{C}}$ for its Galois group. Write $\Sigma(\mathcal{C})$ for the set of prime numbers $p$ such that $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}\in\mathcal{C}$. We prove that, for two such pairs $(K_i,\mathcal{C}_i)$, every isomorphism $G_{K_1}^{\mathcal{C}_1}\simeq G_{K_2}^{\mathcal{C}_2}$ is induced by a unique isomorphism between $K_2^{\mathcal{C}_2}/K_2$ and $K_1^{\mathcal{C}_1}/K_1$, provided that $\Sigma(\mathcal{C}_i)$ has positive upper Dirichlet density for at least one $i$. As a consequence, we generalize reconstruction results of Uchida and Sueyoshi to Galois extensions $\Omega_i/K_i$ such that $\Omega_i$ has no nontrivial abelian pro-$\Sigma$ extension, where $\Sigma$ has positive upper Dirichlet density. We also prove a relative version of the first result without a density assumption: the same conclusion holds if the group isomorphism is compatible with the canonical restriction maps to the maximal abelian pro-$\Sigma(\mathcal{C}_1)$ quotient of the absolute Galois group of $\mathbb{Q}$, and if $2\in\Sigma(\mathcal{C}_1)$ or at least one of $K_1,K_2$ has a complex prime. This relative result applies, in particular, to maximal pro-$p$ quotients under these conditions.
item.dc:creator: Ryoji Shimizu

item.title: Mahler's problem and Turyn polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2405.08281v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mahler's problem asks for the largest possible value of the Mahler measure, normalized by the $L_2$ norm, of a polynomial with $\pm1$ coefficients and large degree. We establish a new record value of approximately $0.951$ in this problem by analyzing certain Turyn polynomials, which are defined by cyclically shifting the coefficients of a Fekete polynomial by a prescribed amount. Recently, Klurman, Lamzouri, and Munsch established that the distribution of values over the unit circle of Fekete polynomials of large degree is effectively modeled by a particular random point process. We extend this analysis to the Turyn polynomials, and determine expressions for the asymptotic normalized Mahler measure of these polynomials, as well as for their normalized $L_q$ norms. We also describe a number of calculations on the corresponding random processes, which indicate that the Turyn polynomials where the shift is approximately $1/4$ of the length have Mahler measure exceeding $95\%$ of their $L_2$ norm. Further, we show that these asymptotic values are not disturbed by a small change to make polynomials having entirely $\pm1$ coefficients, which establishes the result on Mahler's problem. We also estimate that the limiting value of the normalized $L_1$ norm of these polynomials exceeds $0.977$, in connection with a question of Newman.
item.dc:creator: Michael J. Mossinghoff

item.title: Iwasawa theory for unitary groups via Eisenstein congruences and its applications
item.description: arXiv:2410.13132v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime number. In this article, we study automorphic aspects of Iwasawa theory for unitary groups, focusing on the $p$-primitivity of Klingen Eisenstein series and their $p$-adic families on $\mathrm{U}(m+1,n+1)$, which is a key component in establishing lower bounds for Selmer groups in Iwasawa theory for $\mathrm{U}(m,n)$.
