First, we compute the Gan--Gross--Prasad period integral of a Klingen Eisenstein series on $\mathrm{U}(m+1,n+1)$ against a cuspidal automorphic form on $\mathrm{U}(m+1,n)$, and relate it to special Rankin--Selberg $L$-values. We then interpolate these period integrals $p$-adically as both forms vary in Hida families, thereby producing a Rankin--Selberg type $p$-adic $L$-function for $\mathrm{U}(m,n) \times \mathrm{U}(m+1,n)$ as a byproduct. This method is designed to replace the computation of Fourier--Jacobi coefficients used in the existing literature to establish the $p$-primitive property of Klingen Eisenstein series, which so far treats only cases where $m+n \leq 2$. As an application, we consider the case $\mathrm{U}(m,n)=\mathrm{U}(1,0)$ and obtain a new proof of M.-L. Hsieh's Iwasawa main conjecture for CM elliptic curves over a totally real field $F$ with CM field $M$ and good ordinary reduction at all places above $p$, for all primes $p \geq 5$ unramified in $F$. Our approach removes the assumption in Hsieh's original work that $p$ does not divide the relative class number of $MF/F$.
item.dc:creator: Ruichen Xu

item.title: Differential forms and Brauer classes in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2412.01785v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study $p$-torsion Brauer classes in positive characteristic arising from differential forms. We relate this construction to the Brauer group of supersingular K3 surfaces and analyze the contribution of these classes to the Brauer-Manin obstruction. As an application, we examine the Brauer-Manin set of supersingular K3 surfaces and of varieties admitting many differential forms.
item.dc:creator: Domenico Valloni

item.title: Classification of torsion of elliptic curves over quartic fields
item.description: arXiv:2412.16016v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a quartic field $K$. By the Mordell-Weil theorem, $E(K)$ is a finitely generated group. We determine all the possibilities for the torsion group $E(K)_{tor}$ where $K$ ranges over all quartic fields $K$ and $E$ ranges over all elliptic curves over $K$. We show that there are no sporadic torsion groups, or in other words, that all torsion groups either do not appear or they appear for infinitely many non-isomorphic elliptic curves $E$. Proving this requires showing that numerous modular curves $X_1(m,n)$ have no non-cuspidal degree $4$ points. We deal with almost all the curves using one of 3 methods: a method for the rank 0 cases requiring no computation; the Hecke sieve, a local method requiring computer-assisted computations; and the global method, an argument for the positive rank cases also requiring no computation. We deal with the handful of remaining cases using ad hoc methods.
item.dc:creator: Maarten Derickx, Filip Najman

item.title: Shintani invariants and cyclic quantum dilogarithms
item.description: arXiv:2508.18320v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We express general Shintani invariants of real quadratic number fields in terms of cyclic quantum dilogarithms, which appear in the asymptotic expansion of $q$-Pochhammer symbols. We also explain how a formula from 1995 of Sczech for Shintani invariants can naturally be understood in this framework.
item.dc:creator: Bora Yalkinoglu

item.title: Moments of the zeros of Faber polynomials of the Miller basis
item.description: arXiv:2510.05737v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the zeros of modular forms in the Miller basis, a natural basis for the space of modular forms. We show that the zeros of their Faber polynomials have linear moments. By analyzing the moments we can extend the known range of the forms in the Miller basis for which at least one of the zeros is not on the arc - the circular part of the boundary of the fundamental domain. Additionally, for forms in the Miller basis of an index asymptotically linear in the weight such that all zeros are on the arc, we compute the limit distribution of the zeros, which depends on the asymptotic ratio of the index to the weight.
item.dc:creator: Adi Zilka

item.title: On the Least Colossally Abundant Exception to Robin's Inequality
item.description: arXiv:2510.23889v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Robin's Inequality posits $G(n)<e^{\gamma}$ for $n>5040$. Robin also showed that if the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) is false, then $G(n)>e^{\gamma}\left(1+\displaystyle\frac{c}{(\log n)^{b}}\right)$ for infinitely many values of $n$. By analyzing the prime or semiprime quotient $\displaystyle\frac{n}{m}$ for consecutive Colossally Abundant (CA) numbers $m$ followed by $n$ (where $m$ satisfies Robin's Inequality and $n$ violates it), we demonstrate that if the Riemann Hypothesis is false, then the least CA counterexample, $n$, must be constrained to the band $e^\gamma<G(n)<e^\gamma \left(1+\displaystyle\frac{c}{(\log n)^b}\right)$ where $0 < b < 1/2$ and $c\ge\displaystyle\frac{2\operatorname{gpf}(m)+1}{\operatorname{gpf}(m)^{2}}(\log n)^{b}$, i.e. for $c$ satisfying this lower bound, excluded from the infinite set beyond the higher threshold. The lower bound on $c$ tends to $0$ as $n \to \infty$.
item.dc:creator: Bruce Zimov

item.title: Fine-grained deterministic hardness of the shortest vector problem
item.description: arXiv:2511.01626v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\gamma$-$\mathsf{GapSVP}_p$ be the decision version of the shortest vector problem in the $\ell_p$-norm with approximation factor $\gamma$, let $n$ be the lattice rank and $0<\varepsilon\leq 1$. We prove that there is no algorithm that solves $(2-\varepsilon)$-$\mathsf{GapSVP}_p$ uniformly for all $p\in\mathbb{N}$ in time\[ 2^{2^{o(p)}}\cdot 2^{o(n)},\] unless the Exponential Time Hypothesis is false. The proof is based on a deterministic Karp reduction from a constrained variant of the subset-sum problem to $\mathsf{GapSVP}_p$ for fixed $p$. While most hardness results for the shortest vector problem in finite norms rely on randomized reductions, our method is entirely deterministic. As a consequence, we also obtain a deterministic Karp reduction from the standard subset-sum problem to $(2-\varepsilon)$-$\mathsf{GapSVP}_{\infty}$.
item.dc:creator: Markus Hittmeir

item.title: On subradically sifted sums related to Alladi's higher order duality between prime factors
item.description: arXiv:2601.10636v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, I utilize a variant of the Selberg--Delange method to find quantitative estimates of the sums \[M_{k,\omega}(x,y)=\sum_{\substack{p_{1}(n)> y\\ n\leq x} } \mu(n) {\omega(n)-1\choose k-1},\] where $y$ can grow with $x$ but we must have $y\leq Y_0\exp(\mathscr{p}\frac{\log x}{(\log\log (x+1))^{1+\epsilon}})$ with $Y_0,\mathscr{p},\epsilon>0$. Moreover, I give preliminary upper bounds for the general range $1.9\leq y\leq x^{\frac{1}{k}}$. In addition, I formalize the notions of subradical and radical dominance and discuss their relevance to the analytic approach to the study of arithmetic functions. Lastly, I give a fascinating formula related to the derivatives of the gamma function and the Hankel contour, which should be relevant for those employing the Selberg--Delange method to obtain higher-order terms.
item.dc:creator: Yazan Alamoudi

item.title: On the size of $\{a: 1\leq a<n, n|a^2-1, a|n^2-1\}$ for number $n$: Connections to Fibonacci-like Sequences and Twin Primes
item.description: arXiv:2603.17434v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a positive integer n, let $\mathcal{A}(n)$ denote the set of integers $a$ satisfying $1 \leq a < n$ subject to the simultaneous modular conditions \(n \mid a^2 - 1\) and \(a \mid n^2 - 1\). In this paper, we investigate the structural properties and cardinality of \(\mathcal{A}(n)\). By establishing a precise algebraic correspondence between the elements of \(\mathcal{A}(n)\) and the integer evaluations of a family of Fibonacci-like sequences defined by a second-order recurrence, we prove that \(\vert{}\mathcal{A}(n)\vert{} < \log_2 n +2\) for all composite $n > 1$. Trivially, $|\mathcal{A}(n)| = 2$ when $n$ is an odd prime power. Furthermore, we analyze the global distribution of these cardinalities, demonstrating that the asymptotic average of \(\vert{}\mathcal{A}(n)\vert{}\), for $n\leq x$, approaches $2 + o(1)$ as $x \to \infty$. Guided by the properties of the underlying algebraic mapping and supported by computational verification for all $n < 10^{15}$, we formulate the conjecture that $|\mathcal{A}(n)| \le 3$ uniformly for all $n$. In connection with this conjecture, we show that every integer $N$ that is the product of a pair of twin primes satisfies $|\mathcal{A}(N)| = 3$, providing an explicit family of integers $N$ with $|\mathcal{A}(N)| = 3$.
item.dc:creator: Srikanth Cherukupally

item.title: On the Chevalley-Bass number of a field
item.description: arXiv:2604.10802v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give upper and lower bounds on the Chevalley-Bass number of a field of characteristic zero, whenever this quantity is well-defined. We also describe an algorithm which computes the Chevalley-Bass number of a field, provided its maximal abelian subextension is known. As a primary application, we improve the value of a constant related to exponential Diophantine equations.
item.dc:creator: Jean Gillibert, Florence Gillibert, Gabriele Ranieri

item.title: Analogues of the Lindel\"of Hypothesis for the Barnes multiple zeta function and related problems
item.description: arXiv:2606.02407v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Upper bounds for the Riemann zeta function $\zeta(s)$ as $\Im(s)\to\infty$ have been extensively studied in connection with the Lindel\"of Hypothesis. In particular, the Lindel\"of Hypothesis is one of the most important open problems in analytic number theory. It is also known to be equivalent to certain mean value estimates, which provide a fundamental connection between pointwise upper bounds and integral mean values of zeta-functions. In this paper, we consider an analogue of the Lindel\"of Hypothesis for the Barnes multiple zeta function $\zeta_r (s,a,(w_1,\dots,w_r)) = \sum_{m_1=0}^\infty \cdots \sum_{m_r=0}^\infty (a+m_1 w_1+\cdots+m_r w_r)^{-s} $ for $\Re(s)>r$, with $a,w_1,\dots,w_r>0$, and establish equivalent conditions in terms of integral mean values. We treat the rank-one case and, under a polynomial growth assumption on the derivative, the general-rank case. The $\Q$-rank of $\langle w_1,\dots,w_r\rangle$ specifies the region considered in our statements; the equivalence argument itself does not establish that its left boundary is a critical line.
item.dc:creator: Takashi Miyagawa

item.title: Finite-core Volterra reductions for the Riemann phase kernel
item.description: arXiv:2606.29555v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive exact same-sign formulas for a Riemann theta phase kernel and give a Volterra representation with its boundary and integrated tail terms. The formulas apply to finite theta cores, and the boundary-plus-tail identity also holds for the full theta series. We give an outward-rounded fourteen-node counterexample to nonnegativity of the exact endpoint-B form on the active closed-trace core in the original application. Continuity of the defining kernel transfers the negative value to a smooth witness supported outside the trace interval. As a result, the original energy is unbounded below on every nonempty affine trace fiber that retains this vertical direction. We specify a coercive modification and its changed Euler equation. Positivity of the original full-coordinate Weyl kernel and the zeta-facing application remain unresolved.
item.dc:creator: Marvin B. Freedman

item.title: Harmonic weights in inverse central binomial series
item.description: arXiv:2607.09904v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how the partial fraction coefficients of an inverse central binomial series change when the harmonic weight $H_{pn}$ is replaced by $H_{qn}$. For positive integers $p<q$, every coefficient increases. As the index $k$ grows, the increase tends to $2\log(q/p)$ uniformly over all angles $0<\phi\le\pi$, even when the angle approaches either endpoint. The increase is above the limit at every odd index and below it at every even index. We give the first correction, of order $k^{-2/q}$ for $q>2$ and of order $k^{-2}$ for $(p,q)=(1,2)$. For the normalized transforms, subtracting $c$ times the first from the second gives a Stieltjes function exactly when $c\le1$. We also determine which real dilations $0<p<q$ satisfy the same sign law. For $p\ge1$ it holds exactly when $q\ge2$. For $0<p<1$ it holds above a threshold $Q(p)$, and at the threshold it holds precisely on one interval $0<p<p_*$. Finally, we give angle identities at every odd weight from three onward and determine which Dirichlet $L$-terms cancel at angle $\pi/3$.
item.dc:creator: K. Srinivasa Raghava

item.title: A few remarks on the Baez-Duarte Criterion
item.description: arXiv:2607.12084v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study exponentially damped M\"obius approximants in $\mathscr H=L^2([1,\infty),dt/t^{-2})$. With \[ \gamma_n(t)=\left\lfloor\frac tn\right\rfloor -\frac{\lfloor t\rfloor}{n},\qquad f(u)(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)e^{-nu}\gamma_n(t),\] we compute the relevant scalar products, characterize the M\"obius coefficients as the unique coefficients giving pointwise convergence to the constant function, and prove $\langle1 \mid f(u)\rangle\to1$. Vasyunin's formula expresses $F(e^{-u})=\|f(u)\|_2^2$ as an arithmetic cotangent sum. In the final section we give a criterion that would help in the analysis of asymptotics of $F(x)$ as $x\uparrow 1$.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Pyvovarov

item.title: The density of long runs of non-$r$-free integers
item.description: arXiv:2609.09221v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fix $r\ge2$ and let $D_k$ be the natural density of the $n$ such that none of $n+1,\dots,n+k$ is $r$-free. We prove that $\log(1/D_k)=\frac{r-1}{\zeta(r)}k\log k+\frac{r}{\zeta(r)}k\log\log k-C_rk+o(k)$, where $C_r=\frac{1}{\zeta(r)}((r-1)\log\zeta(r)+r-1+r\log\frac{\pi}{r\sin(\pi/r)})$; for $r=2$ this is $C_2=\frac{6}{\pi^2}(1+\log\frac{\pi^4}{24})=1.4595513\dots$. This determines Mirsky's constant $\alpha(h)$, the density of the $n$ with $s_{n+1}-s_n=h$ in the squarefree numbers, to the same precision. Previously the only known estimate was $\log\alpha(h)\le-\frac54 h\log\log h+O(h)$; ours improves this by a factor of order $\log h/\log\log h$, and is two-sided. The upper bound rests on the observation that the primes $p\le z$ with $\prod_{p\le z}p^r\le\sqrt k$ sieve a window of length $k$ with no freedom of alignment, so that at least $(1/\zeta(r)+o(1))k$ positions must be covered by $r$-th powers of distinct primes exceeding $k^{1/r}$. The resulting sum over injections is $m!e_m$ with $m\sim k/\zeta(r)$, evaluated by a saddle point. For the lower bound the Chung-Erdos inequality recovers the full contribution of $m!e_m$ rather than merely its largest term, which is what makes the linear coefficient explicit. As a consequence the first-moment threshold for gaps between $r$-free numbers is $\frac{\zeta(r)}{r-1}\frac{\log x}{\log\log x}(1-\frac{(1+o(1))\log\log\log x}{(r-1)\log\log x})$; for $r=2$ the constant is $\pi^2/6$, that of Erdos's 1951 lower bound. We also prove that every covering system of length $k$ has modulus at least $\exp((\frac{r}{\zeta(r)}+o(1))k\log k)$, so the Chinese remainder construction yields only $\zeta(r)/r$, half of $\pi^2/6$ when $r=2$. Erdos's bound is thus equivalent to the assertion that the first run of $k$ consecutive non-$r$-free integers occurs at the first-moment threshold, not at the scale set by the minimal modulus of a covering system.
item.dc:creator: Xinyang Jiang

item.title: Radial Limits and Euler Exponents of a False Theta Series with Character Modulo 8
item.description: arXiv:2609.18956v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $T_k=k(k+1)/2$ and let $N_n(q)$ be the series with terms $(-1)^{T_k}(2k+1)^{2n+1}q^{T_k}$ for $k\ge 0$. We study the false theta function $D=N_0$ and the moment quotients $N_n/D$. We prove an exact transformation formula for twists of even order. It expresses each moment as a convergent series of derivatives of the Dawson integral, with the dual twist and its phase determined by a quadratic Gauss sum. The formula gives the finite radial values of the moments at roots of unity as nonzero cyclotomic integers and yields congruences between them. Inside the unit disc we consider the quotient of $D$ by the theta series with terms $(-1)^{T_k}q^{T_k}$. Each nonconstant coefficient of this quotient is minus twice a positive integer that counts divisors and restricted partitions. These counts give a Lyndon-word formula for the exponents in the formal Euler product of $D$. The factorization also identifies the unique real zero in $(-1,1)$. A comparison with a cubic polynomial shows that this simple zero is the only zero in $|q|<1/2$.
item.dc:creator: K. Srinivasa Raghava

item.title: Non-degeneracy and Fibering with Applications to Diophantine Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2610.10799v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by applications in Diophantine approximation, we develop a new fibering mechanism for non-degenerate manifolds in $\mathbb{R}^n$, showing that they admit local decompositions into families of non-degenerate curves with uniform quantitative non-degeneracy estimates. Our construction applies to $l$ non-degenerate $C^N$ manifolds under the optimal regularity assumption $N\geq\max\{n,l\}$, requiring no additional smoothness. Furthermore, we show that this uniform quantitative local control can be globalised into a qualitative statement, so that almost every point of a non-degenerate manifold lies on a non-degenerate curve contained in the manifold. The resulting quantitative fibering estimates are also stable under sufficiently small $C^n$ perturbations at each fixed spatial scale. The method provides a framework for extending fibering based results in Diophantine approximation from curves to manifolds. Such applications are considered in the paper.
item.dc:creator: ZiAn Cody Zhao

item.title: Solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ with small $x_3$: a spectral approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.15706v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We count the integral solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ with $|x_3|$ of size at most $M$, for $M$ smaller than $\sqrt D$, using a smooth weight $\Phi(x_3/M)$. Such solutions correspond to binary quadratic forms of discriminant $D$, and hence to geodesics in the hyperbolic plane. Under this correspondence, $x_3$ is small exactly when the geodesic passes close to the point $i$. We count these geodesics by the spectral theory of automorphic forms. Throughout, $\theta=7/64$ is the Kim-Sarnak exponent. For non-square $D=f^2D_0$, with $D_0$ a fundamental discriminant, the geodesics are closed. We obtain an asymptotic formula with error $O(D^{\varepsilon}f^{1+\theta}D_0^{2/3}M^{-1/2})$. The main inputs are the formulas of Duke-Imamoglu-Toth and Baruch-Mao for cycle integrals, the cubic moment bounds of Young and of Andersen-Wu, and a Hecke relation which reduces everything to the fundamental discriminant $D_0$. For $D\equiv 5 \bmod 8$ this counts all solutions, and the range $M\ge D^{1/2-1/1332}$ of Friedlander and Iwaniec improves to $M\ge D^{4/9+\varepsilon}$. For square $D=n^2$ the geodesics run from cusp to cusp, and Hecke theory reduces them to the single geodesic from $0$ to $\infty$. For every $n$ and both parities of $x_3$ we obtain an asymptotic formula with error $O(n^{1+\theta+\varepsilon}M^{-1/2})$, which is non-trivial for $M\ge n^{71/96+\varepsilon}$. This improves the range $n^{5/6+\varepsilon}$ of the elementary method and confirms the corrected main term of the author's earlier work. This paper was written in collaboration with Claude (Opus 5.5, High; Fable 5.2 in the final stage), an AI model developed by Anthropic.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Baier

item.title: Upper Bounds on the de Bruijn-Newman constant for Dirichlet $L$-functions with primitive real-valued characters
item.description: arXiv:2610.27343v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\chi_m$ be a primitive real-valued Dirichlet character of conductor $m\ge3$, let $L(s)=L(s,\chi_m)$ be the associated Dirichlet $L$-function, and let $\xi_L(s)$ denote its completed form. For each $t \in \mathbb R$, we define the entire function \[ H^L_t(z) := \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{tu^2} \Phi_L(u) e^{izu} du, \] where $\Phi_L$ is the superexponentially decaying density \[ \Phi_L(u) := \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \xi_L \left(\frac{1+is}{2}\right) e^{-isu} ds. \] The family $\{H_t^L\}_{t \in \mathbb R}$ describes the heat-flow evolution of $\xi_L$ and solves a backward heat equation. By the work of Newman, there exists a finite constant $\Lambda_L$, called the generalized de Bruijn--Newman constant, such that all the zeros of $H_t^L$ are real if and only if $t \ge \Lambda_L$. The Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for $L$ is equivalent to the assertion that $\Lambda_L \le 0$. Dobner established the matching lower bound $\Lambda_L \ge 0$, while de Bruijn proved the upper bound $\Lambda_L \le \tfrac12$. We prove the unconditional uniform bound $\Lambda_L\le95241/320000=0.297628125$ for every primitive real-valued character of conductor $3\le m\le400$, together with stronger individual bounds. The proof extends the effective approximation of Polymath to Dirichlet $L$-functions, retaining the conductor dependence in the error estimates. We combine these estimates with Platt's numerical verification of GRH and rigorous interval computations. We also give conditional bounds under explicit global initial zero-strip hypotheses, including $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le3/4$ for the zeros of $H_0^L$.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Freire, Cristian Gonz\'alez-Riquelme, Claudio Mu\~noz, Felipe Poblete, Vicente Salinas

item.title: Frangible prime gaps
item.description: arXiv:2610.34525v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A prime gap $(p_n, p_{n+1})$ is \textit{frangible} if the smallest prime divisor of every integer $m$ with $p_n<m<p_{n+1}$ is strictly less than the size of the gap, $p_{n+1}-p_n$. Gafni and Tao recently proved that the number of frangible gaps up to $X$ is $\ll X/\log^2 X$, answering a question of Erd\H{o}s. They also showed that under the Dickson--Hardy--Littlewood prime tuples conjecture this number is $\sim c X/\log^2 X$ for a constant $c$, for which they obtained a rough estimate. We describe improved methods for estimating this constant under the same hypothesis, and establish that its value lies in $[2.74161, 2.79201]$, confirming a speculation of Gafni and Tao. In addition, we present the results of a complete survey of frangible gaps up to $10^{17}$. An ensuing empirical measurement of $c$ matches our estimate very well.
item.dc:creator: Michael J. Mossinghoff, Timothy S. Trudgian

item.title: Inverse powers and 2-adic properties of binary 3 x 3 matrices associated with the Tribonacci sequence
item.description: arXiv:2611.04855v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study binary 3 x 3 matrices with determinant one that generate the Tribonacci recurrence. Starting from a specific generating matrix, we obtain explicit expressions for its powers and inverse powers in terms of the Tribonacci sequence T_n and two associated sequences B_n and R_n. This matrix framework yields identities involving traces, determinants, and products, including addition formulas and Cassini-type relations linking T_n, B_n, and Rn. Moreover, we derive new identities from the matrix representation of inverse powers and establish structural relations between these sequences. As an application, we investigate arithmetic properties of Tribonacci numbers and determine the exact 2-adic valuation of T_2^k for sufficiently large k. Finally, we provide a classification of 3 x 3 matrices associated with the Tribonacci recurrence via similarity over Q.
item.dc:creator: Wilson Arley Martinez, Samin Ingrith Ceron

item.title: A Hypergeometric RM Surface: Integral Monodromy and Level-11 Covers
item.description: arXiv:2611.07849v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Jacobians of a genus-two family with real multiplication by $K=\Q(\sqrt5)$. We realize these abelian surfaces as factors of cyclic-cover Jacobians and determine their integral rank-two monodromy. For the real embedding with $\sqrt5>0$, the projective image is the Hecke group $\Delta(2,5,\infty)$; the conjugate real image is nondiscrete. After a finite base change, we give an explicit degree-four map from Cohen--Wolfart's Hecke cyclic curve to the genus-two curve. Four deck translates of the induced Jacobian pullback give an integral isomorphism from the fourth power of the surface to the eight-dimensional primitive order-$20$ factor, with an explicit nonproduct polarization. At the primes above $11$, the degree-$12$ torsion-line covers are normalizations of quadratic fibre products of genus-one triangular modular curves. We also describe the associated split and nonsplit Cartan-normalizer covers. Finite-field hypergeometric traces give the local Euler factors and a quadratic transformation with a twist by the quadratic character of $2$.
item.dc:creator: Devendra Tiwari

item.title: An Elementary Proof of the Binary Goldbach Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.09007v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the binary Goldbach conjecture which asserts that every even positive integer greater than four can be expressed as a sum of two odd primes. This goal is achieved by proving that the number of ordered Goldbach pairs that add up to $2n$ is an $\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{n}{\ln^{2} n}\right)$ function. As an application, we provide a simpler verification of the ternary Goldbach conjecture that was first established in [6,7].
item.dc:creator: Khaled Qazaqzeh, Aymen Rawashdeh

item.title: Bounding the security of the Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash function
item.description: arXiv:2611.13459v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash functions are a family of Cayley hash functions indexed by an integer parameter $k\ge 2$. Hashes are matrices in $SL_2(p)$ where $p$ is a large prime. We present an attack which finds collisions of length $O(\log p)$ whose average-case time complexity is $O(p^{0.28})$ when $k=2$ and $O(p^{0.36})$ when $k=3$ under an assumption in the spirit of Zaremba's Conjecture on continued fractions. This is an improvement on the more general attacks of Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter which have average-case time complexity $O(\sqrt{p})$. For any $k$, the average-case time complexity of our attack is $O(p^{1-\delta_k+o(1)})$ where $\delta_k$ is the Hausdorff dimension of a certain Cantor set. This tends to $O(\sqrt{p})$ as $k\to\infty$, so our attack has time complexity comparable to Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter's attacks as $k$ grows. We give examples of collisions for large primes found by our attack when $k=2, 3$.
item.dc:creator: Eilidh McKemmie

item.title: Pair Correlation Conjecture for the Zeros of Artin $L$-functions I: Simple and Critical Zeros
item.description: arXiv:2611.20347v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1973, Montgomery posed the pair correlation conjecture (PCC) for the zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Motivated by PCC, Montgomery conjectured that the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function are almost surely simple, and proved that at least $2/3$ are simple assuming the Riemann hypothesis (RH). In 1978, Mueller and Gallagher were able to prove asymptotically $100\%$ are simple assuming PCC and RH. Recently, Goldston et al. noticed that the assumption of RH can be removed in Mueller and Gallagher's method. In fact, assuming PCC by itself without RH is sufficient to prove that asymptotically $100\%$ of the nontrivial zeros are both simple and on the critical line. We adapt the notion of horizontal multiplicity from Goldston et al. to show that the nontrivial zeros of Artin $L$-functions attached to irreducible linear representation of the Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$ are almost surely simple and lie on the critical line without assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH). We will assume the appropriate version of PCC along with some other widely believed conjectures.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Nguyen

item.title: Generalizing the Gaster--Loustau Theorem via Generalized Discrete Markov Spectra
item.description: arXiv:2611.23868v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We realize generalized Markov numbers (GM numbers) for arbitrary $k_1,k_2,k_3\in\ZZ_{\ge0}$ as $\lambda$-lengths of essential simple ideal arcs based at a distinguished cusp of a hyperbolic orbifold constructed from local monodromy matrices. The McShane identity of Tan--Wong--Zhang on this orbifold yields a summation identity with multiplicities for the gaps between the associated Lagrange constants and their limiting value, together with a summation inequality that counts each distinct value once. These results extend the summation identity and inequality of Gaster and Loustau to generalized Markov numbers.
item.dc:creator: Yasuaki Gyoda

item.title: Local-global compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed (co)homology of $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over CM fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.24802v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For each place $v \mid p$ such that $F_v \simeq \mathbf{Q}_p$, we establish a compatibility with $p$-adic Langlands program for completed homology with integral coefficients for $\mathrm{GL}_2$ over CM fields $F$ with $[F:\mathbf{Q}]>2$, after localization with respect to a non-Eisenstein decomposed generic maximal ideal of a Hecke algebra.
item.dc:creator: Jelena Ivan\v{c}i\'c

item.title: On Hilbert's tenth problem over quadratic fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.25002v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 2026, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. In this paper we study Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the quadratic fields $\mathbb Q(\sqrt2),\mathbb Q(\sqrt3),\mathbb Q(\sqrt6)$. Let $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt d)$ with $d\in\{2,3,6\}$. We prove that there is no algorithm to decide for any polynomial equation $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{48})=0$ with integer coefficients whether it has solutions with $x_1,\ldots,x_{48}\in K$. We also show the existence of a polynomial $f(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_{24})$ with integer coefficients such that $a\in K$ is a rational integer if and only if $f(a,x_1,\ldots,x_{24})=0$ for some $x_1,\ldots,x_{24}\in K$.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Wei Sun

item.title: The Riemann Hypothesis and Prime Numbers -- A simple Introduction
item.description: arXiv:2611.25753v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Riemann hypothesis is attracting a great deal of attention at present. It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics, for each of which the Clay Mathematics Institute offers a prize of one million dollars. It is arguably the most important open problem in all of mathematics. Numerous results have so far been proved only under the assumption of the Riemann hypothesis. Yet the hypothesis itself sounds rather dull: it conjectures that the zeros of a certain function have a certain form. Things become truly exciting, however, when we look at its connection with prime numbers, and that is what we shall do here. We give an elementary introduction to the subject.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Rosebrock

item.title: Regulators in the Arithmetic of Function Fields
item.description: arXiv:2207.03461v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: As a natural sequel to the study of A-motivic cohomology initiated in "On the integral part of A-motivic cohomology", we develop a notion of regulator for rigid analytically trivial Anderson A-motives. In accordance with the conjectural picture over number fields, we define it as the morphism at the level of extension modules induced by the exactness of the Hodge-Pink realization functor. The purpose of this article is twofold: first, we prove a finiteness result for A-motivic cohomology; second, under a weight assumption, we show that the source and the target of the regulator have the same dimension. It came as a surprise to the author that the image of this regulator may fail to have full rank, thereby preventing an analogue of Beilinson's celebrated conjecture from holding in our setting.
item.dc:creator: Quentin Gazda

item.title: Arthur packets for metaplectic groups
item.description: arXiv:2410.13606v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For metaplectic groups over a local field of characteristic zero, we define the Arthur packet attached to any Arthur parameter $\psi$ as a multi-set of unitary genuine irreducible representations, characterized by endoscopic character relations. Over number fields, we obtain a multiplicity formula for the genuine discrete $L^2$-automorphic spectrum in terms of global Arthur parameters and $\epsilon$-factors, by leveraging the trace formula for metaplectic groups. This confirms a conjecture of Gan, and extends earlier results of Gan-Ichino on the Shimura-Waldspurger correspondences, whereas their works play a critical role in our proof. Furthermore, all these are shown to be compatible with existing results in rank one (Waldspurger) and two (Gan-Ichino).
item.dc:creator: Wen-Wei Li

item.title: Duality for Arithmetic $p$-adic Pro-\'etale Cohomology of Analytic Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2412.11786v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We prove that the arithmetic $p$-adic pro-\'etale cohomology of smooth partially proper spaces over $K$ satisfies a duality, as conjectured by Colmez, Gilles and Nizio{\l}. We derive it from the geometric duality on the Fargues-Fontaine curve by Galois descent techniques of Fontaine.
item.dc:creator: Zhenghui Li

item.title: A Dyadic Frequency Law for a Perturbed Hofstadter $Q$-Recursion
item.description: arXiv:2603.16111v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the parity-perturbed Hofstadter $Q$-recursion defined by $$Q(1)=Q(2)=1,\qquad Q(n)=Q(n-Q(n-1))+Q(n-Q(n-2))+(-1)^n \quad(n\ge3).$$ for $n\ge3$. Clo\^itre proved that the recursion is globally well-defined and encoded its odd- and even-indexed subsequences by binary arches and canonical plane forests. Let $F(s)=\#\{n\ge1:Q(n)=2s-1\}$, and let $\nu_2(j)$ denote the exponent of $2$ in $j$. For every integer $k\ge0$, we prove the multiset identity $$ \{F(s):2^k\le s<2^{k+1}\}=\{3+\nu_2(j):1\le j\le 2^k\}. $$ The proof expresses frequencies as sums of plateau lengths and folds reflected gap pairs to identify the excess frequencies $F(s)-3$ with the outdegrees of a canonical plane tree. For $k\ge2$, the maximum $k+3$ occurs at $s_k=\lceil 2^{k+2}/3\rceil$, and the second-largest frequency $k+2$ occurs at $s_k+1$. As a corollary, the sum with marks $z^{F(s)-3}$ and dyadic block weights $2^{-ku}$, multiplied by the Dirichlet eta function $\eta(u)$, has the Euler product of $\zeta(u)$ with its factor at $2$ replaced by $(1-z2^{-u})^{-1}$. Finally, we prove that the dyadic defect $Q(2n)-2Q(n)$ attains order $n/\sqrt{\log n}$ in absolute value along a subsequence.
item.dc:creator: Marco Mantovanelli

item.title: Algebraic Hodge generic points are dense
item.description: arXiv:2606.08882v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $f: X \to S$ be a quasi-projective family of varieties defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}} \subset \mathbb{C}$. We show that the points of $S(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ that are Hodge generic for the variation of Hodge structures associated to $f$ are analytically dense in $S(\mathbb{C})$. In fact, in the spirit of the Grothendieck period conjecture and under a large monodromy assumption, we prove the density of the points of $S(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ where the periods of the fibre do not satisfy extra relations 'up to degree $\delta$'. As a by-product, we also establish new instances of the Mumford-Tate conjecture, beyond the realm of abelian motives. When the base $S$ is a curve, we provide quantitative estimates for points satisfying these properties. The main technical contribution is a new result on relations satisfied by solutions of $G$-operators, which relies on height estimates due to Bombieri and Andr\'e.
item.dc:creator: Gregorio Baldi, Gal Binyamini, David Urbanik

item.title: Genus and Gonality of Small Curves, Dynamical Uniform Boundedness, and Bifurcation
item.description: arXiv:2607.12561v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that a complex one-parameter algebraic family of endomorphisms of $\mathbb{P}^N$ has a non-empty bifurcation set if and only if the genus grows superlinearly in degree along every generic sequence of dynatomic curves. In this case, gonality also tends to infinity. In particular, for non-isotrivial families on $\mathbb{P}^1$, gonality tends to infinity along distinct dynatomic curves, while superlinear genus growth holds for every such sequence exactly when the family is not a flexible Latt\`es family. We also establish analogous results for generic sequences of small curves. As applications, we prove uniform boundedness results for iterated preimages over number fields and geometric uniform boundedness results for preperiodic points over function fields. The proof combines arithmetic equidistribution, woven currents, and bifurcation theory. The bifurcation mechanism is what forces the growth of genus and gonality.
item.dc:creator: Zhuchao Ji, Junyi Xie

item.title: An irreducible decomposition of the Weil representation restricted to open compact subgroups
item.description: arXiv:2609.25045v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a $p$-adic field of any residual characteristic, we determine irreducible decompositions of the Weil representation restricted to the maximal open compact subgroups and the Iwahori subgroup by using the Schr\"{o}dinger model. In particular, these decompositions show that the restrictions are multiplicity free.
item.dc:creator: Yuta Takahashi

item.title: An extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37
item.description: arXiv:2611.07138v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct an extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37, resolving the last undetermined optimal minimum in ranks at most 48. The construction begins with the Cayley table of $\mathbb{Z}/13\mathbb{Z}$, assigning a vector of norm four to each cell. We prove that the resulting incidence lattice has exactly 26 unimodular completions of minimum four, all isometric. The resulting Cayley lattice $\Lambda$ has automorphism group $\mathrm{AGL}(1,13)\times C_6$ and is $s$-extremal, with shadow minimum $13/4$ and kissing number $35\,594$. An explicit $4$-frame in $\Lambda$ yields a Type I self-dual $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$-code of length 37 and minimum Euclidean weight 16, resolving the corresponding open case in coding theory.
item.dc:creator: Eric Kubischta

item.title: An asymptotic resolution of the Gao--Thangadurai conjecture on the Harborth constant
item.description: arXiv:2611.19508v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Harborth constant $\mathsf g(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ of exponent $n$ is the least integer $k$ such that every subset of $G$ of size at least $k$ contains $n$ elements whose sum is zero. Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n$. In 2004, Gao and Thangadurai \cite{gt} conjectured that $\mathsf g(C_n\oplus C_n)=2n+(-1)^n$ for all integers $n\ge3$. We prove this conjecture for all sufficiently large integers $n$ and determine all subsets of maximum size in $C_n^2$ that contain no $n$ elements with sum zero.
item.dc:creator: Guoqing Wang, Wenkai Yang

item.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties I. Fibrations over curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.23739v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a number field or the function field of a curve, and let $X\to C$ be a projective fibration over a curve over $K$. We prove a height inequality for relatively nef adelic line bundles $\bar L$ on $X$ with $L$ nef. For a nef, relatively ample line bundle $L$ over a finitely generated field, we deduce a lower bound for the local energy at almost every complex or nonarchimedean realization of a fixed polarized model. Over $\mathbb{C}$, for an ample line bundle $L$ and a smooth positive polarization, the Euler--Lagrange equation is the Calabi--Yau equation. On the projective bundle $X=\mathbb{P}_C(E)$ of a vector bundle $E$ of degree zero, our energy on quotient metrics on $L=\mathcal{O}(1)$ agrees with Donaldson's functional when the determinant metric is fixed. We propose a construction of canonical heights on parameter spaces using envelopes of local energies.
item.dc:creator: Shou-Wu Zhang

item.title: Fourier Bases from Optimal Eigenfunctions of Paley Graphs of Square Order
item.description: arXiv:2611.25727v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $q$ be an odd prime power and consider the Paley graph $P(q^2)$ on the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. A well-known optimal eigenfunction of this graph is supported on the norm-one subgroup, where it takes the values $1$ and $-1$ on the two cosets of its subgroup of index two. Its support has the minimum possible size $q+1$. Starting from this eigenfunction, we construct a family of multiplicative translates and prove that they form a basis of the space of complex-valued functions on $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}^{\times}$. After extending these functions to the whole field, the translates indexed by squares form a basis of one nonprincipal eigenspace of the Paley graph, while those indexed by nonsquares form a basis of the other. In particular, both nonprincipal eigenspaces admit bases consisting entirely of optimal eigenfunctions. The main ingredient is a multiplicative Fourier analysis of the shifted eigenfunction. We determine the moduli of all its Fourier coefficients and, in particular, show that none of them vanishes.
